title: "Vanity URL Prefix"
description: """In DNN 7.1, the ability for users to create vanity URLs was added. This feature cannot apparently be turned off (which should probably also be fixed). But, more importantly here, there is no ability to create a prefix for vanity URLs - they are all at the site root. Nothing then prevents users from """"reserving"""" page names that might later be useful. Also, users can make it look like their vanity URL is a real page on the site. Imagine if google added this and I went and made my vanity URL """"store"""" or """"products"""" or """"****"""" and thus you found my site if you went to google.com/store. That's obviously a terrible idea and no normal company would allow it...  The easiest fix for this would be to make it so administrators can set a prefix for vanity urls. So, instead of example.com/<USER> it would be something like example.com/users/<USER> This way, it's more obvious that this is a user's address on the site.  Without this, it seems dangerous to upgrade to 7.1, which is why I classified it a show-stopper. """

title: "search  security trimming  total result count"
description: """Scenario: There are 45 documents in Lucene (could be modules / pages / docs). They all have the same word, e.g. George. However, the user has view permission on only 5, and suppose these are found on second page (based on ranking) if search is performed as Host. Regardless if user has permission to see the content or not, we always include 'about xx records' as the total hit. For e.g. if Host does the search, he/she will find 45 hits and total count shown in UI will be 45. However, when a typical user does the same search, it will find only 5 hits (based on security) but indicate about 45 records found. I think this is misleading. With security trimming we'll never be accurate as accuracy will result in perf degradation, but we should try to little bit more closer to reality. Given the current collector model for security triming we should be able to exclude the number of records rejected from the total. We should have unit tests to support the above. Note for QA - It's not that easy to write very technical requirement, please come talk to Dev or Ash for more details on this issue."""

title: "DotNetNuke 7.1 Logon Issues"
description: """Hi DotNetNuke Corp, This is an issue we're seeing happen on customers sites that is causing problems. BACKGROUND: In previous versions of DotNetNuke(7.0), """"Login"""" was an acceptable name for a page.  This was great when users had a custom login page. In previous versions of DotNetNuke(7.0), it was acceptable for the login page to be visible to """"Unauthenticated Users"""" but not to """"All Users"""".  This would allow the login page to  disappear once a person logged in. ISSUE: If you have a DNN 7.0 site that has both of the conditions above, upgrading the site to DNN 7.1 breaks all ability to log in.  Fixing the issue requires crawling through a lot of database stuff. RESOLUTION: 1)  Make """"Login"""" an acceptable name for a login page. 2)  Make """"Unauthenticated Users"""" an acceptable level of permissions for the login page/module."""

Notice there are several calls to ThumbnailDownload"""

title: "search  site crawler  module indexer  optimization  LastContentModifiedDate"
description: """Note from CTO: In the core there is a notion of a LastContentModifiedDate for a module. This property is supposed to let the core know of the last date/time that a module modified its content. It has value in a variety of scenarios – including search indexing. The way it is called today I believe is when a module calls SynchronizeContent – which tells the core to expire its module output cache, etc… In the case of search, when the indexer spins through the modules, it should be able to look at this property to determine if it needs to index the content. This would save the additional processing of using reflection to dynamically call the modules GetSearchItems method – only to get back an empty result set if the content has not changed ( which can be a big performance issue, as everytime the GetSearchItems is called the module is internally hitting the database to retrieve the relevant content ). So I would like to find out if we are using this technique. And I realize that not all modules implement LastContentModifiedDate – those that do not would have a value of NULL in this property – which means that in these cases the search indexer would HAVE to call GetSearchItems – but for those that actually do implement it ( ie. Html/Text ) it would produce very good performance benefits."""

title: """Password Retrieval is not enabled"" when accessing WebAPI"
description: """When accessing the WebAPI from the bowser (when not already logged in) you are prompted for you username and password (http authentication) but this fails with a """"Password Retrieval is not enabled"""" error if you configured DNN to store passwords hashed and disabled password retrieval (password retrieval is impossible with hashed password) Password retrieval is no issue here, you're just logging in. Also it is only the setting which causes the problem, not the actual way passwords are stored. Changing the setting, without any change to the stored passwords, will allow you to log in.   Steps to reproduce: - in the web.config, set enablePasswordRetrieval=""""false"""" and passwordFormat=""""Hashed"""". (this only impacts new passwords, existing passwords are unchanged) - Create a WebAPI service and don't allow anonymous access. - Using a webbrowser with which you are not logged in, visit the api url - You will now be prompted for your username and password, enter it. title: "GetUsersByRole Name - Return only Active Users"
description: """GetUsersByRoleName currently returns all users - even those expired in that role. This seems counter-intuitive, but it's used by a few core functions like role management.  I think it would be helpful if there was a core way to get a list of only the current (non-expired) users in a given role. Presumably this could be done by GetUsersByRoleName(RoleName=""""Role"""",IncludeExpired=True), or by adding a new procedure like GetNonExpiredUsersByRoleName. Otherwise, we have to use a linq procedure to re-filter through the result set for active roles, which seems highly inefficient. This is also pretty counter-intuitive. In fact, I found it because a different tool I'd put together was returning too many people so I looked into it. Thanks"""

title: "IE utf8 url referrer-header breaks DNN"
description: """Specificly IE fails to encode the referrer-header to suitable format and passes some invalid data as a result to dnn, which then graciously fails to serve any content with variety of error messages. You may test this by setting a page title with some russian:  """"????????????"""" Which with default friendly url module will return fun enough url, which IE digests well when entering. But as you try leave the page will turn in to myriad of error messages due to IE failing to encode it in to punycode, or whatever the encoding was called. You may observe this by capturing the http request and comparing it to other browsers. Of course this is partly a fail of IE, but certainly DNN shouldn't really be relying on referrer headers in such a way."""

title: "Search  Search Type  Private Property"
description: """We have a concept of SearchType, which maps to a crawler. CE has SearchType 1 for module, PE has 2 and 3 respectively for File and DocumentCrawler. This information is stored in SearchTypes table in database. This information is used by Search Results Settings to build the drop-down for types eligible for public search. By default all searchtypes are listed. There are few exceptions though - Url Crawler and Module Crawler show as Pages (we may need to clean that up though later). However, with this story we want to introduce a concept of Private SearchType. Setting this to true (in database) will make the type to not automatically show up in the above ui (see screenshot). This will help in use cases where we want to search EventViewer or SocialMessages, where these items should not be available by default for public site search. They must be available within the modules only, e.g. Messaging module or Event Viewer module. The only way to test this is to change the setting of File Crawler in database (SearchTypes table), clear cache and make sure it is not automatically selected in search results settings.  """

title: "ContentItems table change"
description: """Hi people,   I’ve been testing my beta DNN Blog module on 7.1 and lo and behold it breaks L. The reason is that I’ve tried using the core framework to the max with ContentItems, Taxonomy etc. Now the ContentItems table has changed. A new column has been added. As my object calls FillInternal, the column is not returned by my view so it unfortunately breaks. The remedy is not that complicated and there is one of many. I can roll my own FillInternal, rewrite the View so it uses * for the ContentItem table, etc. But my point is this: I’m always baffled by how fragile the IHydrateable pattern is. I mean: if the column isn’t there it breaks horribly. Can’t we do a better job? Like provide a more robust method in the core that does not break when a column isn’t there?   Best,  Peter   PS for my own module I solved it with an * in the view, but SQL Mgt Studio always wants to change this back to individual columns when you edit it there. So there is a red flag there."""

title: "DAM  Every user's last selected folder should be remembered"
description: """After using the DAM module for a while, when the user navigates away to a different page on the website, and then comes back to the DAM module page (to perform that one last action that he forgot to do), he sees that he has to again find (in treeview) that folder where he made changes last. That is, the Root folder is set as the selected folder and the treeview is collapsed. This is not very user-friendly. Enhancement request: For each user, the server should remember the last selected folder (probably as a string value for the the folder path). When the user comes back to the DAM module, the module should read this value and make it the selected folder in the treeview (and expand treeview accordingly). The value of """"last selected folder"""" should be stored for every user of the website. It shouldn't matter if the user logged off and logged back in after several days, the last selected folder should still be remembered. Also, when user comes back to DAM module, and the """"last selected folder"""" does not exist anymore (because some other user deleted it), or user does not have permission to view it anymore, or the stored value itself is null or corrupted, then DAM module should not hang and make the Root folder as the selected folder. Nice to have (if we have time): 1. The user's last selected view is also remembered (list, icon, or grid view) -- can be stored as a numeric value. (default to list view) 2. The user's last selected tab is also remembered (Files, Tags, or something else) -- can be stored as a numeric value. (default to Files tab) 3. The user's last selected page size (not page number) (10, 25, 50, 100, or All) -- can be stored as a numeric value. (default to page size 10) This enhancement will make a positive impact in terms of the user-friendliness of the DAM module. The reason is that it will save each and every user of the DAM module some precious time and energy right at the start of the session as he can pick up from where he left off last time."""

description: """I am copying this directly from my posting in the Community Exchange, except that I've added the attachments.    I am a DBA who supports an application using a DNN database. Last week, our production cluster showed CPU usage spiking to 100% for several seconds every 30 seconds, which I traced to DNN's GetScheduledNextTask stored procedure. Our developer then simply truncated the ScheduleHistory table and everything is working smoothly. Discontent on that option as a DBA, I delved further into the issue and found the performance of the current stored procedure appallingly abysmal.    The current stored procedure is this:        The subquery's entire performance is directly dependent on the underlying dataset being extremely small, which is a horrible assumption to make -- any good DBA will tell you that.    ADDED NOTE: We had records in the ScheduleHistory table dating back to February 2012. If you look at the """"Current Stored Procedure"""" image, you'll see the top portion of the execution plan consisting of an Index Scan. That Index Scan was returning almost all the records in the ScheduleHistory table to the Merge Join and to the Sort. There were, at the time, over 200,000 records in the ScheduleHistory table. This is extremely inefficient.    Compare the execution plan of the current stored procedure with the execution plan of the stored procedure optimized:    This has been tested in SQL Server 2005 and SQL Server 2008 R2.    ADDED NOTE: You could also rewrite this as a CTE, but the CROSS APPLY serves the same purpose in this case. title: "Log information when site cannot load correctly during app initialization"

It would help if we logged why we are showing the UnderConstruction page or the 500 error page, so it is easier for admins to troubleshoot issues. There are 4 basic situations:  application is not installed, and both UseInstallWizard and AutoUpgrade are false  log info message """"UnderConstruction page was shown because application needs to be installed, and both the AutoUpgrade and UseWizard AppSettings in web.config are false. Use /install/install.aspx?mode=install to install application. """"   Application needs to be upgraded, and both UseInstallWizard and AutoUpgrade are false  log info message: """"UnderConstruction page was shown because application needs to be upgraded, and both the AutoUpgrade and UseWizard AppSettings in web.config are false. Use /install/install.aspx?mode=upgrade to upgrade application. """"   Database Connection is severed, site is not installed and auto upgrade / useinstallwizard are true  log error """"UnderConstruction page was shown because we cannot ascertain the application was ever installed, and there is no working database connection. Check database connectivity before continuing. """"   Database Connection is severed, site is not installed and auto upgrade  and useinstallwizard are false  log error: """"The connection to the database has failed, the application is not installed yet, and both AutoUpgrade and UseInstallWizard are not set in web.config, a 500 error page will be shown to visitors""""   Database Connection is severed, site is installed  log error: """"The connection to the database has failed, however, the application is already completely installed, a 500 error page will be shown to visitors"""""""

title: "Require Sql Azure Manifest Element"
description: """For sites using SQL Azure as a back-end, we need a way to warn users when a module has not been explicitly tested and verified that it is compatible with SQL Azure. If a non-compatible module is installed, it can prevent backups & restores of the database from taking place, and it can cause run-time exceptions that are not picked up at the install stage. As a pre-emptive measure to protect the integrity of Azure-based installs, we need to add a node to the extensions manifest file, which would essentially be a true/false flag to indicate whether the module has been marked as sql azure compatible by the developer. Upon install, the installer would check to see if it is using SQL Azure as a back end (this can be ascertained by the SQL Version as a query) and then would show a warning message to the user if the module was false or the node was missing, and the database was a SQL Azure database. The user would have to accept the warning and continue in order to install the module."""

title: "Make Social Modules Have Group Settings"
description: """The members directory allows you to set it to show a specific role/group, but the journal module does not. That's frustrating when you want to use social group/activity stuff for existing or fixed groups. As an example, a church website on DNN might already have a """"Members"""" group and just want to set a journal and members directory for those in that group... But, they can't do that without forcing all of their links to apply the GroupID=X parameter for every link going to those pages. Even then, if somebody changed it, it would stop working.  Also, even though the members directory does let you set a specific group, a URL parameter with a group ID actually overrides the setting. So, it would be great if you could set the social modules to use a fixed group and have that work. I suspect this would really help for all sorts of older sites with existing groups - and new sites with established groups.  """

title: "Install Wizard Undesirable Behavior"
description: """When a site does not have connectivity to a database, the behavior of the product is controlled by an AppSetting in the web.config:    <add key=""""UseInstallWizard"""" value=""""true"""" /> When this value is set to True, it invokes the Install Wizard. This is the default behavior and it is set this way in order to make the web-based installation process as simple and smooth as possible. When it is set to False, the application serves the standard Error Page. There are situations that can arise in production environments where a previously installed site can temporarily lose connectivity to its database ( ie. during a windows update of the database server, or a network interruption ). In these cases, if the UseInstallWizard is set to True, all visitors connecting to the site will be redirected to the Install Wizard page. This is NOT acceptable behavior, and in fact is a security vulnerability because the Install Wizard page discloses information about the internal configuration of the site to anonymous visitors. During the installation process, there is currently only one way for the system to know that a site was ever successfully installed previously – and that is by querying the database. Which means that if database connectivity is lost, then the system has no idea if it was ever installed. We need to include another method for the system to know it was installed previously – a method which is persistent and does not rely on external dependencies ( ie. the database or non-core file assets ). We need to introduce 2 enhancements: 1. Add another AppSetting to web.config which will indicate of the system was successfully installed previously. Rather than simply saving a Boolean (True/False) value it would be helpful to store more contextual information such as the version which was originally installed ( this value is already stored in the Versions table in the database but it is more convenient to get access to it in the config file for diagnostic purposes ). This node will only be added to the config AFTER a fully successful installation and will record the core version number of the package that was installed. 2. AFTER a fully successful installation,  the system should change the value of UseInstallWizard to False. There is no valid reason why this value should ever be True after a successful installation, and it would help mitigate undesirable behaviour if its value was set to False. So basically the new logic would be, if there is no database connectivity, the system can then check if InstallVersion <> """""""" – if True, then the system knows that it was already successfully installed previously and should redirect to the Error Page – if False then it would execute the current logic ( checking the “UseInstallWizard” AppSetting, etc… ). This would prevent the Install Wizard from ever being shown in a scenario where the system has already previously been successfully installed.  Note that there is already an “InstallationDate” AppSetting – but this serves a different purpose and cannot be utilized for this solution ( ie. it is used during installation to determine if new MachineKeys have been generated during install – which need to happen as the very first installation step prior to executing any database scripts ). On Upgrade, the system should set UseInstallWizard to False so that existing sites will not continue to suffer from the current behavior. The changes above should prevent the Install Wizard page from EVER being displayed. This will patch an additional issue which exists currently where a site loses database connectivity and visitors are presented with the IntallWizard page, where they can click Continue and if the database has come back online, it will proceed to re-install the application over top of the existing application causing data integrity issues.  """

The skin parsing logic will output the following server tag: <dnn:LOGIN runat=""""server"""" id=""""dnnLOGIN"""" CssClass=""""will-Login"""" Text=""""Sign In"""" LogoffText"""" value=""""Sign Out"""" />  The LogoffText attribute is missing the ="""" and the attribute value.  It is not a well-formed tag. Our parsing logic should be more lenient with additional white spaces to be more usable to for beginners and newbies that are trying to adopt our platform."""

You'll now get the mentioned error mesage. As a workaround you can (temporarily) change the settings in web.config to 'encrypted passwords' and 'allow password retrieval' and add a new site."""

description: """Brief Description of Issue:  If you create a Custom User Property (of type List for a dropdownlist), it is NOT searchable from the Manage Users tool.  Version: DNN 6.2.6 and 7.0.4  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      1.       Create a New Custom Property:  Animal 2.       Make it type: List (so it will be a dropdownlist) 3.       Add 2 Entries for the dropdownlist a.       Entry 1: Text = Cat, Value = 1 b.      Entry 2: Text = Dog, Value = 2 4.       Finish the setup  5.       Edit a User�s profile, and choose �Dog� from the Animal dropdownlist 6.       Search for Users based on the Animal property 7.       Search Dog 8.       Nothing shows up 9.       It only shows up if you search by Value, not by Text   Actual Result:      Cannot search by custom property when it is a List type   Expected Result:       Should be searchable by Text and not just by Value   Fix:  I think there are a few bugs in the UpdateUserProfileProperty stored procedure that is causing you NOT to be able to search for Users by Custom Profile Properties.  In the Stored procedure [UpdateUserProfileProperty] the line is: PropertyText = case when (DATALENGTH(@PropertyValue) > 7500) then @PropertyValue else NULL end, 1. PropertyText is being set to @PropertyValue, instead of the PropertyText. @PropertyText should be included in the stored proc, and this value is stored in the Lists table for Custom Profile Properties. Source code would also need to be modified to add this parameter. 2. PropertyText is being set to NULL if the parameter is LESS THAN 7500. This should be the other way around, I believe."""

title: "admin/Skin/Meta.ascx does not support HttpEquiv and always appends to collection"
description: """The core Meta control (~/admin/Skins/Meta.ascx) offers the ability to specify name and content, but does not expose the ability to specify the HttpEquiv tag (or scheme).  It also does not allow a consumer to insert at the head of the meta collection, which is important in some cases (e.g., for IE7-8 compat mode).   I suggest enhancing by introducing the following properties:        public string HttpEquiv { get; set; }     public bool InsertFirst { get; set; }    And modifying the pre-render handler to read (changes in red):    protected override void OnPreRender(EventArgs e)     {     ...     if ((!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Name) || !string.IsNullOrEmpty(HttpEquiv)) && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(Content))         {         var metaTag = new HtmlMeta();           if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(HttpEquiv))                      metaTag.HttpEquiv = HttpEquiv;         if(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Name))             metaTag.Name = Name;           metaTag.Content = Content;           if(InsertFirst)             Page.Header.Controls.AddAt(0, metaTag);         else             Page.Header.Controls.Add(metaTag);         }     }    Note that because the InsertFirst property defaults to false (and HttpEquiv to null), no new compatibility issues will be introduced by this modification."""

title: "Can not edit page due to bad IconFile path"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:   Since upgrading from DNN 6.x to 7.x we can not enter edit mode on pages of our child portals (it works on the main portal 0) when accessing from a machine other than localhost (Windows  2008/IIS 7.5 environment).   REASON: Bad IconFilePath in Table TabSettings for TabName """"Advanced Settings"""" causes a redirect on the client (see attachment file for details).  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Login to a portal other than the main portal (e.g. portal with id 1)     navigate to a page where you have edit permissions     click on edit page  Actual Result:      DNN redirects to the home page of this portal     the network traffic monitor in the browser shows that an icon was not found (Url: http://www.my.server/Portals/1/~/Icons/Sigma/AdvancedSettings_16X16_Standard.png) and the webserver returns a 302 (it returns a 404 when the same site is being edited locally on the server)  Expected Result:       Page edit mode enabled     no redirection to home page  Details:  We did a clean installation of DNN 7.0.3 and 7.0.4 and checked the database. The IconFile Path is set to NULL on clean installations for the """"Advanced Settings"""" TabName.   The file upgrade.cs (DNN 7.0.3 source) contains a method """"UpgradeToVersion700"""" which adds the bad iconfilepath that our server has.   Interestingly the iconfile path is wrong for all portals but the main portal enters edit mode without any problems."""

title: "UsageDetails problem with multilingual portal"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: The module usage information fails when trying to see in which pages a module exists in Host > Extensions. This works fine in Admin > Extensions. I found where the bug was caused, in the UsageDetail.ascx.cs, property: protected IDictionary<int, PortalInfo> Portals         {             get             {                 if (_Portals == null)                 {                     _Portals = new Dictionary<int, PortalInfo>();                     ArrayList items = new PortalController().GetPortals();                     foreach (PortalInfo item in items)                     {                         _Portals.Add(item.PortalID, item);                     }                 }                 return _Portals;             }         }  The GetPortals() return the result of the SP GetAllPortals, which returns all portals in all languages. Which means my portal names """"XYZ"""" which is using en-US and fr-CA is added twice in the foreach and this causes the bug. Is this fixed in latest DNN upgrades? title: "BLOCKED Export as XML in Dashboard fails when running on SQL Azure"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: If you run DotNetNuke on Windows Azure using SQL Azure for the database, the dashboard will thrown an error when you click the """"Export as XML"""".  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Install DotNetNuke on Windows Azure using SQL Azure db     Go to host/Dashboard page     Click on """"Export as XML"""" button  Actual Result:      Exporting the file will result in error  Expected Result:       The file should be exported without errors.  Code Fix:     IF (EXISTS (SELECT name FROM sysobjects WHERE (name = N'{objectQualifier}Dashboard_GetDbBackups') AND (type = 'P')))        DROP PROCEDURE {databaseOwner}{objectQualifier}Dashboard_GetDbBackups GO   CREATE PROCEDURE {databaseOwner}{objectQualifier}Dashboard_GetDbBackups AS   DECLARE @ProductEdition INT SET @ProductEdition = CAST(ServerProperty('EngineEdition') as INT)   If (@ProductEdition = 5) --Check for SQL Azure  begin   SELECT          'Unsupported' as name,     null as StartDate,     null as FinishDate,     0 as size,     null as database_name,     'UNKNOWN' as BackupType  end else  begin   EXEC('SELECT TOP 20         name,     backup_start_date as StartDate,     backup_finish_date as FinishDate,     backup_size/1024 as size,     database_name,     CASE type     WHEN ''D'' THEN ''Database''     WHEN ''I'' THEN ''Differential database''     WHEN ''L'' THEN ''Log''     WHEN ''F'' THEN ''File or filegroup''     WHEN ''G'' THEN ''Differential file''     WHEN ''P'' THEN ''Partial''     WHEN ''Q'' THEN ''Differential partial''    END as BackupType   FROM             msdb..backupset   WHERE    database_name = DB_NAME()    ORDER BY backup_start_date DESC')  end    GO"""

title: "Control Panel- Module move icon and position menu timing is off"
description: """When a user clicks to add a new module and then hovers the move icon (top-right corner) the move menu slides down. When the user hovers off of this menu the trigger (the move icon) loses it's hover state instantly, or disappears entirely, whereas the move menu pauses for a second and then closes.  This appears disjointed as the two are connected. It is expected that the move icon appears in its active state (white) until the move menu has closed.   The correct order:      The move icon, as black, appears while hovering on the individual module     Hovering on the move icon itself changes the icon to white, and opens the move menu.     Moving the cursor outside the move icon and/or move menu initiates the close animation on the module-move menu     Once the move menu has closed, the move icon (still white) immediately disappears  Attached are 3 screenshots showing current behavior, and 1 screenshot showing desired behavior. current-dragdrop1.jpg : Visually correct until cursor is moved away current-dragdrop2.jpg : Cursor moved to adjacent module, move icon has disappeared before menu has closed current-dragdrop3.jpg : Cursor moved onto move menu, then back to move icon - icon turned black? This should not happen, so long as menu is open, icon should be white and persistent  correct-dragdrop1.jpg : Shows desired behavior - white move icon persistent as move menu closes (disappears when move menu is completely closed), user can hover over other modules while move menu is closing"""

title: "Check Box Rendering"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: The new checkboxes introduced in DNN 7.0.2 are images.  The checkbox images are exchanged with default checkboxes during PageLoad().     We are using the RadTreeView control with checkboxes to present very large TreeViews with thousands of nodes.  Each node is loaded with ContextMenu and other overhead.  To load such a large TreeView were are using the 'Load on Demand' using web services - only the first level is loaded, and then when you expand a child level the information is loaded 'on demand' using a web service call.  The problem is that the child levels do not fire the PageLoad() since using Web Services.  Therefore the checkbox 'trick' DNN is now using does not update the child checkboxes.  The child checkboxes are left in the default checkbox state.  You can see the mixed checkbox presentation that results in the attached image.   Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Open our LMS to a page with the very large TreeView     Expand the TreeView   Actual Result:      Child node checkboxes have older/default checkboxes  Expected Result:      Child node checkboxes should have newer/'trick' checkboxes"""

I understand that these UI changes are for the Admin based panels but they should not be affecting the actual site layout/objects   The UI changes/styles for DNN admin panels should only apply to items in the panels and not to the contents of the site"""

title: "Input File Button invisible"
description: """The default.css file contains a style for the input[type=""""file""""] that completley makes the File button invisible if the skin does not trigger an built in jquery function that would replace the normal button with a Jquery UI version   In addition to making the button invisible, the button is actually active and very large.   This caused big problems on an existing site that I recently upgraded to DNN 7. The public could no longer upload files as the button had gone.   To replicate, just create a skin with only the ContentPane div and an file input object.   When you load the page the file input is invisible   If the input[type=""""file""""] css is removed from the default.css file the file input appears as it should. However when you then login as an Admin, anywhere in the Admin panels that require a file input now also get the Jquery UI   Solution. Create a new css style for file inputs that are used within the DNN admin panels"""

title: "Upgrade causes database to run out of connections."
description: """When upgrading the store from 6.1.3 to 7.0.3 there was a problem with the upgrade. The progress bar was stuck at 0% while the timer continued to increment. After waiting 10 minutes without any progress I looked at the traffic in the 'Net' tab of firebug. I noticed that the web service call was returning an error telling me that the database server had run out of available connections. This error was never handled by the upgrade wizard, which seems odd. I closed the tab to stop the web service requests. next, I closed all active connections to the database. Then I reinitialized the upgrade. While watching the 'Net' tab in firebug, I noticed that the upgrade wizard was issuing requests faster than the server could respond to the requests. This could be the cause of the excessive database connections.   I understand that this could be a difficult issue to reproduce, my suggestion would be to try and upgrade a site where the webserver and database server are distributed across two different machines and/or networks.  Ultimately, to me it looks like the request interval needs to be turned down a little, or it should wait for the first request to return before the next one is issued.  Feel free to contact me if you have any questions about this issue."""

Protected Sub Page_Load(ByVal sender As Object, ByVal e As System.EventArgs) Handles Me.Load         Dim MyBody As Control = Me.Page.FindControl(""""Body"""")         Dim objMyBody = CType(MyBody, System.Web.UI.HtmlControls.HtmlGenericControl)         objMyBody.Attributes.(""""class"""") &= PortalSettings.ActiveTab.BreadCrumbs(0).TabName.ToString.ToLower.Replace("""" """", """""""")     End Sub   Notice that on each page you should see the lowercase tab name as a class on the body tag.  (NOTE: You can just put in a hard coded class here too, just showing my full use case.)   Actual Result:   You get the desired result when not in edit mode, however, when switching to edit mode the class is dnnEditState ONLY and my custom value is gone :(  Expected Result:   When in edit mode I would assume the class would be something like this   class=""""mypagename dnnEditState""""   where mypagename is the value added by my code, and dnnEditState is the one needed for DNN edit mode.   (FYI this works properly pre DNN 7.0!)"""

title: "Error in ModuleActions.js causes module buttons to stay away"
description: """Found with UVG (Video) and SunBlogNuke:   On line 44 of ModuleActions.js an error is raised (can not replace on undefined).   It causes the management functions to stop working.   For defensive programming purposes, I would recommend an approach such that a malfunctioning module can not cause the module management of DotNetNuke itself to stop working.   As a workaround, I have changed:   var paneName = modulePane.attr(""""id"""").replace(""""dnn_"""", """""""");   into       var x=modulePane.attr(""""id"""");    var paneName;    if (x!== null && x !== undefined)    {               paneName = x.replace(""""dnn_"""", """""""");    }    else    {      paneName = x;    }    Now it works always in our 7.0.2 environment."""

title: "Module Container Command results in 'A potentially dangerous Request.Path value was detected'"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  When using a site with popups (dnn6 +) and older style module containers (dnn5 ish) then using one of the 'command' menu items at the bottom of the container will result in the following error, if the page name contains non-ascii characters.   """"A potentially dangerous request.path value was detected from the client (%)""""  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Assign a module to use a container from DNN 5 era (Minimal Extropy will do)     Change the page name to use a name with non-ascii characters - some examples are japanese (???????????) or Icelandic (Fors��a).       Click on the container controls (settings/edit/whatever) shown on the module container (not the DNN7 floating menu)     The popup will show the yellow screen of death with the above error.  Actual Result:           A potentially dangerous Request.Path value was detected from the client (%).     Description: An unhandled exception occurred during the execution of the current web request. Please review the stack trace for more information about the error and where it originated in the code.           Exception Details: System.Web.HttpException: A potentially dangerous Request.Path value was detected from the client (%).  Expected Result:  Popup shown normally   The cause is that during the creation of the popupUrl, the characters within the Url (which are generated from the page name) are Url-encoded twice.  The first encoding takes it to the hex representation (ie http://example.com/%E3%81%8A%E5%AE%A2%E6%A7%98%E3%81%AE%E3%82%B1%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9%E3%82%B9%E3%82%BF%E3%83%87%E3%82%A3/tabid/90/ctl/Module/ModuleId/469/Default.aspx?popUp=true), and the second encoding changes the encoded value into a broken Url, ie http://example.com/%25E6%258A%2580%25E8%25A1%2593%25E8%25B3%2587%25E6%2596%2599/%25E3%2581%258A%25E5%25AE%25A2%25E6%25A7%2598%25E3%2581%25AE%25E3%2582%25B1%25E3%2583%25BC%25E3%2582%25B9%25E3%2582%25B9%25E3%2582%25BF%25E3%2583%2587%25E3%2582%25A3/ctl/Edit/mid/1233.aspx?popUp=true   The double encoding is caught by the asp.net security checks.   The fix is to remove the double encoding which is occuring on the code which loads the module command menu."""

title: "Chrome on Ipad/Iphone. Cannot login"
description: """Hi Folks,   Using Chrome on my Ipad I am unable to login to my DNN 7 site.   Apparently this is because .NET does not recognise the Chrome iOS browser and therefore down levels it to one that does not support javascript. Therefore Postbacks are not supported. I can easily replicate this on login screen.   I was able to fix the problem by creating a browser definition file (CriOS.browser) in the /~App_Browsers directory   <browsers> <browser id=""""CriOS"""" parentID=""""Safari""""> <identification> <userAgent match=""""CriOS"""" /> </identification>  <capabilities> <capability name=""""browser"""" value=""""CriOS"""" /> <capability name=""""ecmascriptversion"""" value=""""3.0"""" /> <capability name=""""javascript"""" value=""""true"""" /> <capability name=""""javascriptversion"""" value=""""1.7"""" /> </capabilities> </browser> </browsers>    Apparently upgrading to .NET 4.5 fixes the problem but I was unable to try that."""

title: "Fix ""Memory"" Page State Persistence Option"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:       ViewState takes up an incredible amount of bandwidth, especially on some of the Admin screens. This can be a performance hit, especially for mobile devices.     The """"Memory"""" Page State Persistence option does not work well with Ajax calls, and does not work with some of the custom DNN controls (CheckBoxes, ComboBoxes) used in the Admin screens.      """"Memory"""" persistence breaks the Site Settings Admin screen.  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Host > Host Settings > Advanced Settings > Performance Settings     Set """"Page State Persistenct"""" to """"Memory.""""     Admin > Site Settings     Click """"Update.""""  Actual Result:       """"Object reference not set to an instance of an object"""" error occurs on multiple lines in SiteSettings.ascx.cs, starting at line 1249. Values being returned from the form are null.  Expected Result:       Site setting should be saved.     No ViewState field in the page source.  Recommendation:   When I was a Core Team member several years ago, I suggested and submitted code to do this. It involved one line in web.config, about three lines of code in Default.ascx.vb, and one small file in the App_Browsers folder. This solution had no issues with Ajax calls, and all controls in the site played nice with it. I took the code directly from Microsoft's ASP.NET best practices documentation.    This was assigned to others in the Core Team to investigate and to develop. Normal procedure. What they produced was a complicated caching approach involving new classes and a hundreds of lines of code. It worked, but it broke Ajax.   I protested, but this approach remained in the core. The """"fix"""" was to put a warning message on the Host Settings page that """"Memory page state persistence can cause Ajax issues."""" That message remains to this day.   Now today, not only does it still break Ajax, but it also breaks value returns from many of the custom DNN web controls.   I submit the following code snippet as a permanent fix, to be included in Default.aspx.cs. This approach puts ViewState in the Session.     private const string PREF_KEY = """"VIEWSTATE_""""; protected override void SavePageStateToPersistenceMedium(object state) { //base.SavePageStateToPersistenceMedium(state); //Store it in session (the base does it in a hidden field)  HostController hc = new HostController();  if (hc.GetHostSetting(""""PageStatePersister"""") == """"M"""")       Session[PREF_KEY + Request.RawUrl] = state; else       base.SavePageStateToPersistenceMedium(state); }   protected override object LoadPageStateFromPersistenceMedium() {     if (hc.GetHostSetting(""""PageStatePersister"""") == """"M"""")    {       object state = Session[PREF_KEY + Request.RawUrl];       //If the object is not in memory, the method tries to get it from the hidden field       return (state != null) ? state : base.LoadPageStateFromPersistenceMedium();    }    else       return base.LoadPageStateFromPersistenceMedium(); }        THIS IS ALL THAT IS NEEDED! You can drop all the existing Memory persistence caching code. KISS.     The use of """"Request.RawUrl"""" is for per-page uniqueness, and could be controlled by a simple setting. If false, then persistence operations would be """"normal."""" If true, then persistence would be per page. The user could leave a page, then return to it before Session timeout to find it as it was left.     This does not break Ajax, because it uses the normal ASP.NET persistence mechanisms.     Performance is greatly enhanced.     This could easily be made a Portal-level setting.          In testing, this does not work with the SiteSettings page, and causes a non-breaking error when loading new modules in Host > Extensions. It's unclear if this is from the design of those pages, or from some of the DNN custom controls in Site Settings. Either way, those pages/controls should be modified to work with Memory persistence. (In testing, I just test for /Admin/ or /Host/ in RawUrl, to determine where to save the page state. Then ViewState is stored in the page source for Admin and Host screens.)  Code snippet adapted from http://www.campusmvp.net/a-better-way-to-persist-viewstate/, from a Microsoft MVP."""

title: "Changing the name of a page in a foreign language (ADMIN) is not taken into account"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:    The modification of the name of a page with ADMIN > Page management is not persistant (it's not retained/stored)      Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Create a bi-lingual installation (fresh DNN 7.0.0)     Enable content localization (Host + Admin > Languages)     Switch to French (or any other language)     Go to ADMIN > Page Management (in french)     Change the name of a page, Update (seems to be ok)     Refresh the page or navigate the page or go to ADMIN > Page management: the name of the page has not been stored....  To modify it, you need to EDIT the page.    DV FX   Install DNN 7.0.2 --> SOLVED THE PROBLEM."""

description: """Anyone involved in DNN Support will probably be able to corroborate this. title: "Multiple versions of Display On All pages modules"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: DNN 6 and DNN 7: When exporting Page Templates with Display On All Pages function applied to modules, every time the Page Template is imported, the modules are repeated again on the page. So if you create 10 new pages with the same page template, you'll get 10 clones of the modules that are Displayed On All pages. It was fixed at some point. But, now again, we are seeing it with DNN 6 and DNN 7.   This is a huge problem for customers using our Page Templates to create DNN their websites as our Page Templates include modules that are Displayed On All pages. It's also a big issue for some of our clients that are tying to build their websites and running into the same issue with modules being inadvertently cloned multiple times on the same page after importing a page template."""

title: "Smarter Exception Logging"
description: """A simple and non-critical error in a frequently running task can easily flood the exception log. This has two detrimental effects: 1. It is very hard for end users to determine errors in the system when this happens as the frequent error obscures any other errors. 2. The error log size can bring down the system.   I suggest we decouple the log itself from the moment the error occurred and log the latter in a separate table. The exception logic would need to check for the specific error first. This could be done by storing a hash of the error and using that as unique key in the error log table. And then recording hash and time in the new table.   Then, in the error log UI give the user 2 view options: 1. Show errors sequentially as they occurred (i.e. as it is now) 2. Show the most occurring errors in descending order   Peter"""

Clear Steps to Reproduce: Step 1:  Implement and load a module with RadGridView with client-side binding. Actual Result 2:  The RadGridView scrollbar differs from other scrollbars (page, divs)   Actual Result 3:  To fix the above problem in an easy way DNN core should be changed, what is not recommended.    Expected Result 1:  Data within RadGridView after client-side binding should be well formatted.  As DNN is a platform supporting Telerik components, all their component features should work as Telerik has predicted without major workaround.    Expected Result 2:  All elements on the page should look the same.   Expected Result 3:  Default (.css, js�) settings should contain only contain the basic settings that holds together the page. Other (non essential) features should be implemented in the skin. This is the approach Telerik is using for their components. They claim that with this approach the skins are not version dependent, what I find annoying in DNN.     Thank you for considering my suggestions."""

title: "DAL 2 - Use of PetaPoco Query method"
description: """Late in the 7.0 development cycle it was realised that many of the methods of the DAL 2 use PetaPocos Query method.  As this method keeps the reader open while iterating through the return IEnumerable (as it uses the yield break syntax, it means that the context cannot do any other command during an iteration over the returned IEnumerable.   PetaPoco provides the Fetch method which does a ToLIst() call before returning the IEnumerable thus allowing the reader to be closed.   Some uses of Query were fixed - but a few remain to be fixed."""

title: "Allow cursor .cur files to be included in package without file restriction alert"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  When a module package includes a cursor .cur file, the DNN installer shows a warning about restricted file and causing the user to back off from completing the installation of the module. The cursor is a harmless file and is very useful to improve the usability of the UI. E.g. there's a need to show the zoom cursor to enlarge an image but this can only be done using a cursor file for cross-browser compatibility. Referencing a custom .cur file is a CSS standard and should not have an ill effect.  https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/CSS/cursor   Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Include a .cur file as part of a module package.  Actual Result:      DNN Installer will show a warning about restricted file upload.  Expected Result:       It should allow .cur files since it's harmless and is part of CSS2 standard."""

title: "Desktop modules cannot have a version numbers where any part is greater than 99."
description: """Information for Desktop Modules is stored in the 'dbo.DesktopModules' DNN table. One of the columns in this table contains the desktopmodule version number, saved as a string.   This is in the format of Major.Minor.Revision, and is padded with leading '0's so that 3.5.90 becomes 03.05.90  for example.   There is a similar column in 'dbo.Packages', except the version there is padded with leading '0's.   The bug occurs when attempting to install a module with a version number in which one of the parts is over 99, say 3.5.120. In this case, the version number is truncated to 03.05.12 in 'dbo.DesktopModules'.    The reason for this, is that the 'Version' column is limited to 8 characters maximum. There is no limitation of this sort on the Version column in the 'dbo.Packages' table (50 characters).   The fix for this is to update 'dbo.DesktopModules' so that the version column allows more than 8 characters, as well as the associated stored procedure 'UpdateDesktopModule' so that input parameter 'Version' is more than 8 characters in length."""

title: "A returnurl query string parameter should take precedent over the ""Redirect After Login"" setting"
description: """If there is a """"Redirect After Login"""" page specified for a portal, this setting takes precedent over a returnurl query string parameteter .    The problem, to me at least, is as follows:   Certain modules, such as bring2mind's document exchange, send links to their location (for instance for direct downloads) through mail or other means. If the page is only visible to certain users or roles and the user is not logged in, DNN's default behaviour kicks in and a login mask is presented.   A returnurl parameter is added to the page's querystring, however, if the administrator has specified a """"Redirect After Login"""" page, the user will be redirected to that page, instead of the url specified within the returnurl parameter.    Maybe you could also just create some portal settings that allow administrators to better control the login behaviour of a portal."""

description: """Brief Description of Issue: Just discovered two bogus entries in our test site's PortalAlias table. Both are entries consistent with attempts to use the site as a proxy. See Screenshot1.jpg (attached).    Here are some details:       UserID fields' values (-1) indicate that the record was not entered by a logged-in user through the Site or Host admin screens.     Date field values were set consistent with entries in the IIS logs, rather than being null. This seems to indicate that this was accomplished by somehow calling """"EXEC AddPortalAlias."""" title: "Entity Framework DB Access Causes Web Site to Hang"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: I have built several modules and two scheduled tasks for DNN 6.2.4, using ASP.NET 4 and the Entity Framework, rather than DNN's built-in data layer. The strange thing is that it all worked well until I published one of the scheduled tasks. The web site would simply """"hang."""" The browser would not time out. No error pages. No log entries (system, database, or DNN event log). I created a new database, and it would connect and run fine. Simply change the connection string to point back to the first DB, and it would fail. I downloaded DNN 7 beta, which also failed in the same way.   I am completely stumped as to why nothing at any level would throw an error or log an event.   Finally, I removed the Entity Framework connection strings from web.config, and the problem went away. I added them back in, one by one (a connection string for each module), until it failed. Again, it was for one of the scheduled tasks. (It is a task that fetches data once a day from the National Weather Service, and stores it locally for use by a weather module.)   I submit this as a """"heads up,"""" as Microsoft seems to want us to use the Entity Framework now. I don't know if the Core Team has any plans to upgrade to EF or not. Personally, I love it. It can make module development and deployment much simpler, without needing SP scripts.  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      I can submit code to you, if you wish. Nothing here that I can't trust to the Core Team.  I have attached my web.config. The connection string that causes the error is the one that is commented out. I have tested this connection string multiple times, and it is correct.    Again, submitted as a """"heads up."""" Something you may want to look at, and may want to inform users of as a potential problem. I leave it up to all of you."""

title: "digest authentication not thread safe"
description: """see this forum thread for the full details and suggested resolution  http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Forums/forumid/160/postid/471758/scope/posts.aspx#471758   Copied from above thread:                                                         In short: code in the digest authentication area blows up when under heavy load.             Testing out my app which uses web service to make a large number of requests (it gets through about 10 requests per second solidly over several minutes), it was ok with just one client device, but when running multiple clients simultaneously, I would - guaranteed - see """"Internal Server Error"""" (http status 500).             Using IIS7 request tracing got the following as the culprit:             [CryptographicException: Hash not valid for use in specified state.]              System.Security.Cryptography.CryptographicException.ThrowCryptographicException(Int32 hr) +41              System.Security.Cryptography.Utils.HashData(SafeHashHandle hHash, Byte[] data, Int32 cbData, Int32 ibStart, Int32 cbSize) +0              System.Security.Cryptography.Utils.HashData(SafeHashHandle hHash, Byte[] data, Int32 ibStart, Int32 cbSize) +57              System.Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithm.ComputeHash(Byte[] buffer) +51              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DigestAuthentication.CreateMd5HashBinHex(String val) +106              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DigestAuthentication.GenerateUnhashedDigest() +156              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DigestAuthentication.AuthenticateRequest() +158              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DigestAuthenticatorImpl.TryToAuthenticate(HttpContextBase context, Int32 portalId) +206              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DnnController.AuthenticateRequest(HttpContextBase context, Int32 portalId) +145              DotNetNuke.Web.Services.DnnController.Initialize(RequestContext requestContext) +183              System.Web.Mvc.ControllerBase.Execute(RequestContext requestContext) +56              System.Web.Mvc.<>c__DisplayClass8.<BeginProcessRequest>b__4() +58              System.Web.Mvc.Async.<>c__DisplayClass1.<MakeVoidDelegate>b__0() +20              System.Web.CallHandlerExecutionStep.System.Web.HttpApplication.IExecutionStep.Execute() +453              System.Web.HttpApplication.ExecuteStep(IExecutionStep step, Boolean& completedSynchronously) +371              Interestingly,  I found this comment on http://code.google.com/p/jsonfx/sourc... :              """"fixing 2nd most common exception: CryptographicException """"Hash not valid for use in specified state.""""              - System.Security.Cryptography.MD5 must be in a critical section if accessed from multiple threads""""             And lo and behold, here is DotNetNuke.Web\Services\DigestAuthentication.cs :                           private static string CreateMd5HashBinHex(string val)              {               byte[] bha1 = Md5.ComputeHash(Encoding.Default.GetBytes(val));              .... etc...              }                           Funnily enough, the JsonFx.NET formerly looked like this:                           byte[] hash = MD5HashProvider.ComputeHash(value);                           and the fix was to replace with:                          byte[] hash;             lock( MD5HashProvider)              {              hash = MD5HashProvider.ComputeHash(value);              }                           Looks pretty similar to me.  And this is happening under high load when quite likely two requests might be trying to authenticate at the same time, so makes absolute sense.             Incidentally the client software is in Java using Apache HttpClient (Seen from Android 3.2 and 4.1, I think the Android 4.0 tablet just got lucky so far).  That's a solid toolkit with a good reputation.             I suspect my recourse may be to compile my own DNN, which does not please me in the slightest!  I'm posting this in advance of going down that path, so although this is a likely fix, it does need testing.             Probably fix is of course to do:             lock(Md5) {  bha1 = Md5.ComputeHash(Encoding.Default.GetBytes(val));  };             Any comments gratefully received.             I don't know if this will affect DNN7 or not: maybe in backward compatibility areas. Sorry, I do not have time to look into that aspect, this will need to go in production using 6.2.something.             <USER>            Cornerstone Software Ltd"""

title: "Adapt the installer to any prior present language pack"
description: """In 7.0.0 the installer will download a pack on demand if you select one of the supported languages to install. If a language pack had been dropped into the distribution beforehand this is installed and then overwritten by the downloaded pack if that language was selected.   We (DNN INT) suggest the following changes to the logic:          If there is a language pack in the Install/Language folder it should appear on the dropdown to install.     This augments the core distributed available packs. So if there is a de-DE pack in the install folder, then show the de-DE from the mothership labeled as officially supported     If there is just one zip file in the install folder, then make this the default to install  This should also allow non-supported languages to be rolled out to customers by integrators *and* would allow us to test packs."""

title: "Improve performance of UserRoles table through a change in indexing"
description: """I'm not 100% sure of this but from what I know the performance of the UserRoles table could be enhanced if we change the indexing and get rid of the false PrimaryKey. Certain customers (read: those with many users and roles) complain about performance of this piece.   Currently we have UserRoleID as primary key and unclustered index. The field serves no purpose at all in the framework other than as primary key to the table. IMO this field would need to be deprecated. Instead the key (and hence unclustered index) should be UserID, RoleID. Given that this is probably the most oft used direction (it would help my app in any case). Alternatively it could be RoleID, UserID. But the way it is doesn't make sense to me."""

title: "Default settings"
description: """For new installations, there are always a number of steps I follow to optimize DNN. I think at least some of them should be default for a new installation. So perhaps these are some things you might consider for new default settings: - disable some of the items in the eventlog configuration. - disable skin widgets - perhaps try and set the sites timezone to the correct time zone - set default user registration to 'none' instead of 'public', I think this really is a potential security risk. - set check for upgrades to false by default - set the superuser title to the name/title of the site you just created instead of DotNetNuke - set the superuser portal url to the portal you just created, instead of the www.dotnetnuke.com - set the superuser e-mail address to the e-mailaddress of the superuser you just created - disable the DotNetNuke copyright part by default - set the module cache provider to memory (I don't know if this might cause problems with some providers) - set the scheduler method to Timer by default  - configure some of the scheduled task items better:  - set the search indexer to once or twice a day  - increase the purge schedule history to run about every 2 hours, to keep the table nice and small, especially since the new messaging dispatch will run every minute. And since the history will only be cleaned up every day, it will fill up to 1 x 60 x 24 = 1440 items until it is cleaned. Even though it says it should keep only 10 items."""

title: "Eventlog table"
description: """When you look for ways to improve the performance of DNN, a tip which is seen a lot is """"Clean out the eventlog table"""".   It seems there once was a task in the scheduler to Purge the Event log. The stored proc. even exists for this task ([PurgeEventLog]).   It also seems there is/was an issue with this scheduled task as you can see here: http://blog.laksha.net/2009/03/purgeeventlog-cause-sql-blocking-in.html   and here: http://support.dotnetnuke.com/issue/ViewIssue.aspx?ID=10868&PROJID=2   So for such an important optimization step for DNN, I think it is strange that it is not something that has had any attention. So I think it would be a good thing that: 1) if there still is a problem with this sp, someone should take a look at it, and improve it. Perhaps first check the rowcount, and if it is above 2000, delete everything above that number or something. 2) add the item back to the scheduler again for new installations."""

title: "Global Error Handling"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  Large customers like the Department of Defense use AKAMAI for content delivery. AKAMAI relies on standard HTTP error codes for determining how/when to cache content. DotNetNuke traps unexpected errors within the global.asax handler ( DotNetNuke.Web.Common.Internal.DotNetNukeHttpApplication ) and displays a """"friendly"""" error page - ErrorPage.aspx in the root of the website.  The system returns an HTTP 200 status when it displays the custom error page rather than the actual HTTP error code. This confuses AKAMAI.  The system should trap the error and dispay a custom page, but it should still send along the original HTTP error code generated rather than a 200."""

title: "codeSubDirectory Deployment Issue"
description: """When DotNetNuke installs a module with files being deployed into App_Code, it adds a codeSubDirectories node into the web.config. The purpose of this node is to allow class files written in different languages to be compiled into independent assemblies. However, it is not possible to add a subdirectory more than one level below the App_Code directory ( http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-US/Library/54dwfbb7(v=vs.90).aspx ). If you declare an entry more than one level below App_Code ( ie. <add directoryName=""""test-folder\test-child"""" /> ) .NET will throw an immediate YSOD run-time error: �Only subdirectories directly under the App_Code directory are allowed�. The standard convention for dynamic DotNetNuke modules is for the App_Code folder structure to match the DesktopModules folder structure � where we support multiple levels of nested folders ( ie. /DesktopModules/OwnerName/ModuleName ). If you a deploy a dynamic module which was written using nested folders, DotNetNuke will create an invalid codeSubDirectories node ( ie. <add directoryName=""""OwnerName\ModuleName"""" /> which results in an immediate unrecoverable crash of the application. DotNetNuke does need to support dynamic modules written in both C# and VB, so the codeSubDirectories logic is important. However the installer logic needs to be modified so that it only declares one level of folder structure. In the example above, it would declare <add directoryName=""""OwnerName"""" /> even though the code files are deployed to App_Code/OwnerName/ModuleName. This instructs .NET that all subfolders under the App_Code/OwnerName folder are written in the same language ( which will be the case 99% of the time anyways ). If a developer tries to use mixed language code files in the subfolders, the system will throw a run-time error informing them of this problem. Dynamic Modules using our recommended folder structure and packaged using the native Extensions Packager will not install properly into another DotNetNuke installation until this change is made."""

title: "Global Error Handling - Custom Error Page"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  Large customers like the Department of Defense use AKAMAI for content delivery. AKAMAI relies on standard HTTP error codes for determining how/when to cache content. DotNetNuke traps unexpected errors within the global.asax handler ( DotNetNuke.Web.Common.Internal.DotNetNukeHttpApplication ) and displays a """"friendly"""" error page - ErrorPage.aspx in the root of the website.  The system does not provide any customization of the custom error page - which is problematic in Enterprise environments that need to completely obscure the platform being used on the back-end.   The system should be enhanced to allow for an errorpage.html file which can be stored in the portal home directory. When an error occurs, the system should first look for this errorpage.html file and if it exists, serve the contents of this file within the errorpage.aspx. This allows for portal-level customization."""

title: "PUSHED FROM 7.0 - SQL Azure Support"
description: """When trying to install third party modules or even do custom development in DotNetNuke, there are syntax differences in what is supported in SQL provisioning scripts on SQL Azure as opposed to standard SQL Server. In total, there are many syntax differences between the 2 database platforms, however there are a few syntax differences which are extremely common and can be dealt with in an automated manner:  When DotNetNuke executes SQL script as part of installing an extensions ( or via the Host / SQL module ) the system should look for the following common SQL Azure syntax pitfuls and intelligently """"fix"""" them ( *note: that in """"fixing"""" these issues, it does not affect the ability of the script to execute on standard SQL as well, as these syntax items are NOT required ): Remove �ON [PRIMARY]� Remove """"TEXTIMAGE_ON [PRIMARY]"""" Remove �WITH ( � )�  So basically if we take the following sample SQL script: CREATE TABLE [dbo].[MyTable](   [MyTableId] [int] IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,   [Field] [nvarchar](50) NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT [PK_MyTable] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED ( [MyTableId] ASC ) WITH (PAD_INDEX =OFF,STATISTICS_NORECOMPUTE=OFF,IGNORE_DUP_KEY=OFF,ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS =ON,ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS =ON) ON [PRIMARY] ) ON [PRIMARY] We should convert it to:  CREATE TABLE [dbo].[MyTable](   [MyTableId] [int] IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,   [Field] [nvarchar](50) NOT NULL,   CONSTRAINT [PK_MyTable] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED    ( [MyTableId] ASC ) )  The SQL script above will execute successfully on SQL Azure and Standard SQL Server. By """"fixing"""" these common syntax issues we could likely expect a 75% increase in the number of modules that can successfully install on SQL Azure - without requiring any modifications on their part.  As part of this enhancement, there is already code in the Host/SQL modue which logs the actual script executed against the database in the EventLog. If we modify the script to remove the syntax issues above, we should write the converted script content to the EventLog to allow for simpler debugging measures."""

title: "Advanced Settings  Installing multiple items together"
description: """In the new Advanced Settings window that we have introduced in 7.0, the user would most likely want to install multiple items at the same time.  Example use cases: Install multiple Language packs at the same time Install multiple Authentication Systems at the same time Install multiple Providers at the same time Install multiple Optional Modules at the same time   The user just went though installing the Dotnetnuke before seeing the Advanced Settings screen. Asking the user to install one item at a time is not very convenient for the user.   Installing multiple items: User checks the language packs he wants to install (say german, spanish and italian) and leaves others unchecked (dutch, french). User then clicks the install button on the bottom and goes through the install wizard just once for all 3 languages packs that he wants to install. That is, he accepts just one Combined License and the install log will show the installation steps for all 3 language packs together. Upon clicking the return button, the user will go back to Advanced Settings and may install multiple auth systems/providers/modules together.   I raised this as an enhancement because currently, it is very tedious to install things in advanced settings. The user has to step through a wizard, accept license and install for every item. By the end of it, the user is left with very little energy/motivation to install another item. This was originally suggested by <USER>in issue http://support.dotnetnuke.com/issue/ViewIssue.aspx?id=22739&PROJID=52   I strongly believe we should implement this enhancement. Also, if we choose not to implement this, then there isn't much different between Advanced Settings and Host Extensions. User can easily close Advanced Settings and do the same thing in Host Extensions. Advanced Settings is only useful if it speeds up the Superuser's job of installing extensions for this new dotnetnuke installation."""

title: "Member Directory Displays Non-Portal Users"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  This problem affects multi-portal installations of DNN.  By default, the Member Directory displays users who match this criteria:  PortalID = [current portal] OR PortalID IS NULL.  This logic is in the GetUsersAdvancedSearch stored procedure.  The problem is that the NULL matches (1) super-user accounts who should not appear in the results and (2) deprecated users who are not affiliated with any portal.   Clear Steps to Reproduce:       Use a host-level account to add an extra portal to an existing DNN installation.     Add several users to the extra portal.     Return to the default portal.      Delete the extra portal.     Add the Member Directory to the default portal.   Actual Result:       The Member Directory shows super-users on every portal's Member Directory.     The Member Directory shows deprecated users.  These are not super-user accounts.  They are users that should have been removed when a portal was deleted, but instead their records are left in the database unassociated with a PortalID.   Expected Result:      The Member Directory should not show super-users in any portal.  Or perhaps an option could be available in the settings to allow super-users to be displayed.     The Member Directory should never show deprecated users.  Community Feedback I am not the only user to have experienced this issue.  See the following community discussions for other examples: http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Community/Community-Exchange/Question/1570/DNN-6-2-member-directory-and-social-authentication-not-limited-to-portal.aspx http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Community/Community-Exchange/Question/1522/Why-member-directory-showing-all-users-from-all-sites.aspx"""

title: "Services API should allow alternate specification of portal alias"
description: """The services layer attempts to load the DotNetNuke context by string parsing of the domain name.  While this is satisfactory for applications already running in a DotNetNuke context, external applications might not be aware of the http-alias associated with a given request (and instead have a portalId or portalAliasId).   It would be useful for those external applications to be able to make calls into the service layer, and as such I suggest that -- when domain name parsing fails -- an additional attempt to load the DotNetNuke context be made using the querystring and portal alias id.   Alternately, it would be just as useful to all a consumer to use a portal alias id in the URI path, rather than only allowing a HttpAlias.  E.g.:   http://dotnetnuke.com/999/DesktopModules/Journal/API/Services/List   For example,    protected virtual void LoadDnnContext()   {   var domainName = TestableGlobals.Instance.GetDomainName(ControllerContext.Request.RequestUri);   var alias = TestablePortalAliasController.Instance.GetPortalAliasInfo(domainName);    if(alias == null) alias = LoadAliasFromQuerystringOrHeaderOrOtherInterestingLocations(context.Request.QueryString[""""PortalAliasId""""]);     if(alias != null)     { ... }   else     throw ...;   }    This change would make it a lot easier to consume services from external applications, where less might be known about the request initiator."""

title: "DnnApiController.LoadDnnContext does not protect against invalid aliases"
description: """In LoadDnnContext (DnnApiController.cs on or about line 84), an attempt is made to load the portal alias:    var alias = TestablePortalAliasController.Instance.GetPortalAliasInfo(domainName);   ValidateTabAndModuleContext(alias.PortalID, out tabId);    Note that the alias is immediately dereferenced (via alias.PortalID). title: "Base href for tokenized email is invalid"
description: """In SendTokenizedBulkEmail.cs on or about line 486, a base URI for embedded images is calculated as:    body = """"<Base Href='"""" + PortalAlias + """"'>"""" + body;   Here the PortalAlias is of the form """"dotnetnuke.com"""" after being hydrated with the HTTPAlias property (see line 248). title: "Removing All Deleted Users"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:   If a site that has a million users and tries to remove all deleted users (say 100 of them). the operation will be be very costly and likely never complete.   Details   The current function is based on a foreach() of every user in the portal to determine if the user has been deleted before performing the complete removal   Because of the foreach() of every user it will hydrate an info object, including their profile, for every user in the portal. If User Online status monitoring is enabled it will fire that event off several times as well.   Other performance concerns are that RemoveUser() clears the cache after every user deletion. Which is great for 1 user but could be very taxing constantly refreshing the cache for every user that is deleted.       Possible Solution:   We have to implement a method to cut to the chase and just get the isDeleted flagged users from the database and remove them."""

title: "Module CSS Field"
description: """I think it would be good if modules had a CSS class field that was applied to their outer div.    Say I want to have some announcements modules that are """"special announcements"""" that are styled differently. How do I do that? Right now, the only way is to specifically add entries to my page CSS for every announcements module that I want to be styled differently. But, that would be counter to half the point of CSS. If I had a module-level css field that was automatically applied to the outer wrapper, then I could just put in """"specialAnnouncements"""" and then add that class to my portal css.    This is really about making sure that site administrators can do things they want without having to hope that module developers follow some practice... and, in this case, module developers wouldn't need to just add a wrapper, they would need to create their own setting for the css class applied to that wrapper - and that's a dumb requirement to push to module developers when the core wraps modules in a div anyway."""

title: "Social API should support GetRecommendedRelationships and GetClosestRelationships operations"
description: """It would be very useful (both from a core standpoint and within individual modules) to be able to support the identification of potential relationships and  """"closest"""" relationships.  The former is heavily used within the Facebook UI, and it would be great to be able to mirror that within a DNN installation.  The latter is generally used to transmit """"important"""" notifications in e-mail dispatches and similar.   Both would need to be generated on a schedule, and should be extendable via a provider-based interface.  This would allow the community version to utilize something simple (e.g. K-means clustering) and allow more advanced algorithms to be applied where useful.  A provider-based system would also be important for tractability, as the analysis for large user bases would likely need to be offloaded (e.g. as an Amazon EMR job) for performance reasons.   It would be very simple to implement this in a minimally-optimal manner, and would likely increase the use of social functionality on dotnetnuke.com.    Note that, ideally, each function should be partitioned by NotificationType.  So, it would be possible to GetClosestRelationships(user, RelationshipController.Instance.GetFriendsRelationshipByPortal(portalId)) to just identify closest friends, or GetClosestRelationships(user) to identify a set of all closest potential relationships."""

title: "Consider additional methods to identify relationships between two principals"
description: """There appears to be no good way to identify the set of relationships between two principals.  While it is possible to enumerate union of each principal's individual relationships, this is not an efficient operation (in particular, it requires loading the potentially large number of relationships for one user).   I suggest pushing this query into the database and introducing two overloads, which would read similar to:   ISet<UserRelationship> GetRelations(UserInfo principal, UserInfo other); ISet<UserRelationship> GetRelations(UserInfo principal, UserInfo other, bool bidirectional);   Obviously for .NET 3.5 compatibility an IEnumerable would be used over ISet.   A bidirectional search would return the union of relationships from a->b and b->a.     Advanced social functionality really requires this sort of query be very, very efficient.  Accordingly, I'm elevating the severity."""

title: "Sitemap priority not saved correctly in culture with comma as decimal seperator"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  If your server that hosts DNN is configured with culture that uses a comma as a decimal seperator instead of a dot, then sitemap priority isn't saved correctly.  The cause is simple, the fix also.  Cause:  The textbox with the value is loaded like this:     txtSitemapPriority.Text = tab.SiteMapPriority.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); So with InvariantCulture. Fix: change line 661 of tabs.ascx.cs from     tab.SiteMapPriority = float.Parse(txtSitemapPriority.Text); into     tab.SiteMapPriority = float.Parse(txtSitemapPriority.Text, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); And the problem is fixed."""
