description: """Brief Description of Issue:    Original issue posted on Forum http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Forums/forumid/200/threadid/462796/scope/posts/threadpage/1.aspx      After Upgrade a 6.2.1 instance to DNN 6.2.2 try to open the login page gets   a popup square shows """"Error Code: 500 Internal Server Error. Note: Web servers receive requests that are URL encoded. This means that certain characters may be replaced with a percent sign (%) followed by a particular number. For example, %20 corresponds to a space, so a request for http://myserver/My%20Dir/My%20File.htm is the same as a request for http://myserver/My Dir/My File.htm. Normalization is the process of decoding URL-encoded requests.  Because the % can be URL encoded, an attacker can submit a carefully crafted request to a server that is basically double-encoded. If this occurs, Internet Information Services (IIS) may accept a request that it would otherwise reject as not valid. When you select Verify Normalization, the HTTP filter normalizes the URL two times. If the URL after the first normalization is different from the URL after the second normalization, the filter rejects the request. This prevents attacks that rely on double-encoded requests. Note that while we recommend that you use the Verify Normalization function, it may also block legitimate requests that contain a %. *Source: http://www.microsoft.com/technet/isa/.... title: "Core Messaging Replies to Roles."
description: """Brief Description of Issue: If an administrator sends a message to a role (ex. Registered Users) there is multiple issues that arise.   1. No way to opt out of receiving these messages. This could be a setup issue so users don't send to Registered Users but to a Subscriber role that users can opt in and out of. However it would be interesting if they could opt out emails from any specific role AND a global setting for opting out of ALL email notifications.   2. When a user replies to a message they received from the admin that was sent to a role. The CoreMessaging_Messages table will say: """"TO: Registered Users"""". I believe this should say the name of the administrator that it was sent too. Not the role name   3.  and contain the same ConversationID as the original message. This will mess up the user messaging interface and make it complicated to see all the messages properly threaded.      When a user replies to a message sent to a role. It should create a new conversation that goes specific back to the sender and copies in the Subject and body. This will solve problems if multiple users reply to the original message.    Alternatively I would recommend a more verbose threading option for Role group messages where it shows the original message and then a sub thread of any user that replies with any back and forth responses between you and that user."""

title: "DNN 6 partial page rendering breaksTelerik reporting"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: We have a module that uses Telerik's reporting API (Telerik.Reporting.dll, Telerik.ReportViewer.WebForms.dll). After upgrading DNN from 5.6.1 to 6.2.1, we discovered that the records quit showing up in Telerik's report viewer. (I could still see the report viewer, but no records were showing.) After much investigation I was finally able to fix it by disabling the """"Supports Partial Rendering"""" for that user control. The user control itself does not have ajax functionality in the code, so there shouldn't be a conflict between the user control and the DNN framework's built-in partial page rendering. I am guessing this might be a bug introduced in DNN 6 b/c the report works fine in DNN v5.6.1 with partial page rendering enabled.  Han"""

title: "ClientDependency Framework causes non-visible controls to be databound"
description: """As a DotNetNuke module developer, I'd like it if code used by the DotNetNuke framework did not walk the ASP.NET control tree, so that my modules containng non-visible databindable elements are not DataBound before I want them to be, which causes bugs and performance issues.  Clear Steps to Reproduce:      Create a new DotNetNuke module.  This module should contain:              A ListView         A DataSource               Set Visible=""""false"""" to the ListView     Add a breakpoint to the Select method being called via the DataSource     Run the module in a DotNetNuke site in debug mode  Expected Result:      The breakpoint is not hit because the select method was not called     Actual Result:      The breakpoint is hit, because the select method was called  Root Cause:   The Client Dependency Framework contains an extension method, FlattenChildren.  This extension method is being called during Page PreRender.  This extension method and its caller are walking the entire control tree.  As a result of the entire control tree being traversed, any control in the tree that's databindable is being databound.  At best, this causes performance issues, as Service / Presenter methods are called unintentionally, and at worst, this would cause bugs, because the datasources may not have enough contextual information to call the Service / Presenter methods correctly."""

title: "Globals.GetURLType should recognize other common URI schemes"
description: """In Globals.cs on or about line 2783, the method GetURLType attempts to differentiate between the different TabTypes.   This method correctly identifies schemes in the set {mailto, http, https} as being of TabType.Url, there are other schemes that should be similarly categorized.   By way of example, the URI """"javascript: alert('')"""" is misidentified as being of type TabType.File, and subsequently incorrectly attached to the LinkClick handler.    I suggest expanding the schemes correctly identified by this method to include: javascript, geo, im, sms, tel, doi, git, magnet, skype, sftp (schemes in bold are the """"important"""" ones)   Note that a more general solution would identify (or attempt to identify) all valid IANA schemes in addition to common unofficial schemes.   An argument could be made that the method correctly identifies URLs and ignores URNs; however, this is not the case for the mailto scheme, and the result is both unintuitive and produces results that are suboptimal (e.g. TabType.File for URNs that are better identified as being URL than as a file)."""

title: "Telerik File Manager unusable w/ many users & files"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: When you open any text/html module and click on the add an image icon and are presented with the Telerik image File Manager it will just spin for 15+ minutes and will likely timeout.   I believe the issue has something to do with a site that has many users the telerik file manager will load the /Users/ folder and by doing so will pull all the individual permissions for each of those users personal files.   It may also simply be an issue with a vast amount of files in the file manager.   After doing some profiling I was able to see that it's not an issue of SQL calls. The application will only make a couple SQL calls then it will do the rest of the data crunching within the application before it returns a result.   Example of the SQL order of operations    exec dbo.GetFolders @PortalID=NULL exec [sp_procedure_params_100_managed] @procedure_name=N'GetFoldersByPermissions',@procedure_schema=N'dbo' exec dbo.GetFoldersByPermissions @PortalID=25,@Permissions=N'READ',@UserID=879860,@FolderID=-1,@FolderPath=N''   --Returns 13,000 rows   -- Long Gap (Time where Telerik is just spinning)  exec dbo.GetFolderPermissionsByPortal @PortalId=25   --Final call before it shows results.   I haven't determined if the DNN File COntroller is doing all the work or if it's the data being passed to the telerik code that it is crunching all the data."""

title: "Cache methodology does not handle caching of null values"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: The current caching methodology followed within the DNN core goes something like this     var cache = DataCache.GetCache(strCacheKey); if (cache == null) { cache = DataProvider.Instance.ExecuteSQL()..}     This method can have a negative impact on performance if the requested value from the database returns null (or an empty dataset).    Since the cache value will remain null then it will always go to the database to check the value. null is still an answer to the request and should be saved as such.   This can be seen throughout the DNN core but is most evident in FileController() where a file can be deleted but other settings (page settings, module settings, 3rd party modules) store the FileID and will request a file that no longer exists but will hit the database to find out if the file exists (n) times because it wasn't cached that you already know it doesn't exist."""

title: "Poor performance in ModuleControlController.GetModuleControlByControlKey and ModuleControlController.GetModuleControlsByModuleDefinitionID"
description: """Both functions identified above exhibit poor performance.   GetModuleControlByControlKey:   This is an O(n) operation, where n is proportional to the number of total module controls that exist within an installation.  This operation that is executed several times per page request.   This operation should be backed by a dictionary keyed by control key and definition, with cache invalidation triggered by a change to a module control.   GetModuleControlsByModuleDefinitionID:   This is also an O(n) operation that generates a dictionary on a per-call basis. title: "Cloud Storage - Speed up initial synch"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  Currently, the initial synch with Cloud Storage (Azure or Amazon S3) takes very long to complete. Over 15 minutes for 750 files. Main reason is the redundant http calls. If there is one folder in cloud with 1000 folders, provider makes 1001 calls, first call to get a list of all the files, and then 1 call for each file to the cloud to get meta data. Interesting point to note here is that the very first call to get a list of all the files already has all the metadata information that the subsequent call to individual file calls. The provider simply discards the initial data. We need to introduce temporary cache on the result from the very first call and use that in the subsequent calls. This cache should be temporary, say 1 or 2 minutes, or else the force synchs won't be able to update metadata changes on the cloud (very edge case). It'll still catch new files created, won't clear the deleted files on cloud if cache is too long."""

title: "Performance Issue with GetTabs procedure"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  My current site has 899 portals with 153603 tabs. When GetTabs get executed for one of the portals it takes nearly 15 seconds to execute to return 191 tabs. I don't think server configuration is going to be that much of difference, my test SQL server is having 6 cores with 12gig RAM.  For each time tab is created or module is added tab cache for portal is cleared. This trigger GetTabs 3 times - list of tabs for portals, tab paths for portal and overall portal path cache (regardless of portals). Because of this, upgrade process is nearly impossible to finish in a day.  I dig bit more and found new WITH statement employed for TabPath and Level is core reason for performance degrade."""

title: "Partial Update Error with RadAjaxPanel and AjaxControlToolkit"
description: """There are ongoing problems still with DotNetNuke 6 and the Ajax Control Toolkit. As one of the most popular toolkits, this incompatibility seems to be presenting a lot of developers with considerable heartache.   According to Telerik's own documentation, (http://www.telerik.com/help/aspnet-ajax/troubleshooting-radscriptmanager.html)  the way to get the latest Ajax Control Toolkit to coexist with the latest Telerik controls (and therefore DNN 6), is to use the .NET 4.0 assemblies for both and turn off script combining. We have carried this out by calling the following in page load.   CallByName(DotNetNuke.Framework.AJAX.ScriptManagerControl(Me.Page), """"EnableScriptCombine"""", CallType.Set, False)   This does get rid of the most commonly reported error which is the following: Microsoft JScript runtime error: AjaxControlToolkit requires ASP.NET Ajax 4.0 scripts. Ensure the correct version of the scripts are referenced. If you are using an ASP.NET ScriptManager, switch to the ToolkitScriptManager in AjaxControlToolkit.dll.   However, it then appears to break the RadAjaxPanel which means the partial updates stop working in DNN6.   We have managed to fix this by editing \UI\Modules\ModuleHost.cs in the main DotNetNuke.dll library and reverting to the standard update panel as shown below.  We have tested DNN 6.2 fairly thoroughly with this change and it doesn't seem to have any adverse effects. title: """Time Machine"""
description: """I did search for this, but it is hard to know what others may have called this feature I'm looking for.  We call it the """"Time Machine"""" feature. I've worked on other sites in the past where we've implemented a feature where we can specify the date we want to render the site for.  This allows us to make changes to the site that won't go live for another couple of weeks, but our clients can check out and review those changes by specifying a parameter in the URL. That's how we do it now.  Page at a time.  It works but... What I'd like to see in DNN is a feature that would allow us to let people with specific roles set the date they want to render the site for in a toolbar similar to (or maybe the same toolbar) as the admin toolbar. With the current functionality that I'm aware of, in order for our clients to be able to see what the site is going to look like in the future, we have to setup a staging site where we make the changes and then copy stage to production when the new site is approved. This is awkward at best.  Having this feature implemented would effectively eliminate our need for a staging site for all but code changes."""

Clear Steps to Reproduce:       Install DNNGlobalStorage (     http://www.evotiva.com/downloads.aspx)     Browse to the File Manager     [Manage] > Manager Folder Types     [Add new Type]     Configure e.g. an Amazon S3 provider     Click on [Update]     Back to the """"Folder Type Definitions"""" dialog, the mapping is not there     If you try to add it again (same name), you get an error """"A mapping with the same name already exists. The changes have not been saved.""""     Therefore, DNN is saving the configuration data, but it is not being displayed.      I mean, in the """"FolderMappings"""" table, the row was created. However, in the     """"Folder Type Definitions"""" dialog you just see the standard 'Standard', 'Secure', and 'Database' folder types."""

title: "CountryListBox LookUpCountryCode by IP does not work"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: The CountryListBox control is supposed to automatically set the country based on the user's IP address.  It is not working at all.     Clear Steps to Reproduce:       Register for a new account with country as a property.  Actual Result:       The country field will not be set.       Expected Result:       Country field should be set to user's country.      Code Issue: In the CountryListBox project, the CountryLookup class contains an error in logic. Code Fix: Change line 116 to be (Also attached with this one change):                if (_Address.Length == 4)"""

title: "Mobile Redirection creates redirection loop and does not pass Query String"
description: """We have a mobile site that is (sadly, at the moment) non-DNN and its url is www.mycompany.com.au/mobile . When I redirect the (DNN based) website home page (www.mycompany.com.au) I get an infinite redirection loop. The reason is that when DNN begins a request it sets the current Tab to the Home page if there is no specific Tab requested. In the Mobile redirection interface the code looks at the current tab and queries the redirection data and determines that this Tab is to be redirected. So, in my case, it finds that the Home page is to go to /mobile/default.aspx (remember a non-DNN page) and the Mobile Redirection code then does a response.redirect to it. This is fine - so far. But here's the crunch - since it is a new request and DNN has no specific Tab requested it sets the currentTab to the Home page and then asks the redirection interface if this tab is to be redirected and we have an infinite redirection loop. Fortunately, the code changes required to fix this and the addition of Query Params in the redirection call are all in the MobileRedirectModule.cs module (Library\HttpModules\MobileRedirect\MobileRedirectModule.cs) and are fairly simple. To correct the infinite loop I look to see if the request is for a DNN page and if not then I exit the Mobile Redirection call since DNN only redirects it's own pages to Mobile pages. And to include the Query Params I rebuild the QS without the TabID param as this confuses DNN (the redirection is to tabid=XX but the query param is for tabid=YY and DNN doesn't know which tab to create) and append it to the redirection URL. I have attached an updated copy of the MobileRedirection.cs file. PS this report is based on a forum post so there is slightly more info there. Here is the post link http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Forums/forumid/108/threadid/453426/scope/posts.aspx"""

title: "Client Resource Management removes ""data"" Urls'"
description: """If you're running the composite files option with client resource management, and using data url's to reference images in your css, the CRM removes the """"data:"""" text from the URL.   What are data URLS? More information can be found here: http://www.websiteoptimization.com/speed/tweak/inline-images/  Basically, they are references to files within the CSS instead of URL's to a web server (http:).   See this file to see what I mean: http://cl.ly/0q3G1y1Y2K0K2n2w0z1D   This issue has been reported to the ClientDependency framework project, of which CRM depends on (and is the highest voted on item.) http://clientdependency.codeplex.com/workitem/13196   I think I found the culprit and a fix:   ClientDependency.Core.CssFileUrlFormatter.TransformCssFile seems to be doing the job of cleaning up URLs to work in a combined file, fixing references. The problem is the regex is also picking up data: protocol urls.   Replacing this regex - url\((.+?)\) - with this regex - url\(((?!(""""""""|')data:).+?)\) - will filter those out. (Basically, it's performing a negative lookahead, if the found value contains """"data:"""" it is ignored.)"""

title: "Google Authentication Provider Bug with Multi Language Site"
description: """Fresh install of brand new DNN 6.2.0 CE en-US only  Clear Steps to Reproduce:   Configure in Admin > Extensions > Authentification Provider > Google Authentication projects well configured (AppId and secret) and enabled it.  In google API console, we have to set Redirect URIs (http://www.domain.com/login.aspx and http://www.domain.com/register.aspx) to make it work (if not, google give a mismatch Redirect URI).  In Admin > Site Settings > User Account Settings set to True the """"Use Authentification Providers""""  Test, Work well, can register, and login with google accounts (Clear cookie each time).  Remark : Login and register links always point to www.domain.com/login.aspx and /register.aspx wathever the page you are.  Next step :  In Admin > Languages > Add new language > select one (French in my case) and update. Enable it in language managment.  You'll see the two flags appered next to Login / logout  Logout, clear cookie, and try to login with a google account.  You get a redirect_uri_mismatch in my case , from getting started (the configured home) http://www.mytestdomain.com/GettingStarted/tabid/55/ctl/Login/language/en-US/Default.aspx did not match a registered redirect URI  from the our services page, the uri mislatch is : http://www.mytestdomain.com/OurServices/tabid/58/ctl/Login/language/en-US/Default.aspx  If you register the URI in google API it works, but We can't reasonnabily register in google API all the pages*language as soon as a site have other language(s).  the """"problem"""" is in the url build for login and register in multi language case.   A good solution could perhaps be to build url like in monolanguage, http://www.mytestdoamin.com/en-US/login.aspx, http://www.mytestdoamin.com/fr-FR/login.aspx etc for any language enabled.  Same for register.aspx  Like that we only have two new URI per language to register in Google API.  Regards"""

title: "Months ago, Days ago, Hours ago, Minutes Ago not translatable"
description: """In the global shared ressouces, the MonthsAgo, DaysAgo, HoursAgo and MinutesAgo keys cannot be translated in some languages.   """"2 days ago"""" in french is """"Il y a 2 jours"""" So the key should include a {1} that gets replaced by the number to allow easier translation.   So: """"{1} days ago"""" would translate to """"Il y a {1} jours""""   The key name should also be replaced in the next version so that it is clear to translators in a new version that there is something new to translate there after this modification is done."""

title: "Idea for DNN on user profile"
description: """One thing I notice in DNN is that if there is some settings for personalization of a module settings per user the developer is having to develop an interface and provide a link to it in the module.  In general this gives a very inconsistent interface for DNN (for an example look at the Forum module - editing your signature is done in the module but the edit profile link takes you to the profile page) My suggestion is that DNN create an interface for the profile module/functionality much like the settings interface. So when I have a profile setting for a module (like the signature in the Forum module) it is given a specific control KEY when editing the module control. The profile module would then look and see if there are any controls with that specific KEY  for the modules that are on any pages. Then pull that control and present it as a tab in the edit profile link of the profile module. I think would be a boon to module developers and to DNN overall.  On the UI side it would make DNN appear more 'tied together' and for developers it would give a more specific standard to use for user personalization controls.   I have no idea how this would be accomplished but hope it will be looked at"""

title: "Move DefaultPage.IsPopup into Common.Globals (or Skin.SkinInfo)"
description: """There appears to be no good way to determine if a page is being loaded as a popup.  The only relevant implementation exists within DefaultPage.IsPopup, but this functionality is private (and the instance is not easily accessible).   Suggest moving this function into a statically-accessible context such as Common.Globals or as an instance method on Skin.SkinInfo.  Note that if the latter route is taken (which is stronger), it should be much easier to obtain a reference to the current SkinInfo instance (most skin values are still exposed as strings).   Suggest implementation as (assuming Common.Globals):    public static bool IsInPopUp { get     {     return HttpContext.Current != null && HttpContext.Current.Request.Url.Query.Contains(""""popUp=true"""");     } }"""

title: "Site does not display in IE 9 if user has Helvetica font installed on computer"
description: """Fresh install of I believe any version of DNN will result in Internet Explorer 9 switching to compatibility mode and displaying a blank white page if the user viewing the site has the Helvetica font installed in IE 9.  I believe this is a result of a bug in Internet Explorer and not DotNetNuke.   Clear Steps to Reproduce:  1. Install any version of DotNetNuke - Confirmed with latest 06.01.05 install.  2.  Ensure you have the Helvetica font installed on your computer.  3.  Browse to the site in Internet Explorer  Actual Result:  1. Internet Explorer switches to compatibility mode, but only displays a blank white page.  Expected Result:  1. Internet Explorer would display the page appropriately.  To fix this on a per site basis, you can remove all references to the Helvetica font in the various DotNetNuke style sheets.  To fix this for any and all sites that use Helvetica, you can uninstall the font from your computer.   You can read more about this issue at the following site: http://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/ie/forum/ie9-windows_7/internet-explorer-9-wont-display-some-websites/8f4e6cad-3c4f-e011-8dfc-68b599b31bf5   Note: If this issues has already been reported, I apologize.  I searched through numerous pages of bugs on support.dotnetnuke.com and did not see this one listed."""

title: "canonical URLs cause module detail pages to removed from google index!"
description: """DNN support canonical URLs for some time now.  This is a nice feature, however it can lead to detail pages not being indexed by searchengines, for example consider the DNN blog which uses """"detail pages"""":  http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs.aspx  If canonical URL was setup in URL site settings, DNN would add the code below to the page header: <link rel=""""canonical"""" ref=""""http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs.aspx""""/> The blog entries are available using the URLs below:        http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs/EntryId/3370/Development-and-Test-DotNetNuke-Installations-and-Search-Engines.aspx     http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs/EntryId/3369/Peer-Code-Review-ndash-Are-they-worth-the-hassel.aspx     etc  these are not real DNN Tabs, instead the detail content is displayed based on the EntryID parameter.  However since the TabID is the same, the canonical url is the same for all these detail pages:  <link rel=""""canonical"""" ref=""""http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs.aspx""""/>  This means that Google will only index http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Blogs.aspx and remove all detail pages from the index! title: "Recycle Bin"
description: """The DotNetNuke Recycle Bin offers limited functionality.  Adding additional information and functionality would improve the usability of this feature.  Adding sortable columns of data to the recycle bin would allow users to more efficiently restore the correct page or module to the website.  The problem/Issue:  1. Searching through the recycle bin is cumbersome and slow when it contains numerous (100+) items.  2. Because modules titles are not required by DotNetNuke, finding a module in the recycle bin that was not properly titled is nearly impossible with the current functionality.   Actual/Desired Result/Functionality:  1. The ability to sort the pages or modules deleted by the Page/Module Name, Module Type, Date Deleted, Date Created, or Deleted By User would be very helpful to quickly find the correct item.  2.  Adding the ability to preview a page or module via a modal pop up would give the user the ability to ensure they are restoring the correct item before actually having to restore said item.  Please see screenshots included with this enhancement request."""

title: "Form Pattern doesn't allow real buttons as actions"
description: """Line 337 of default.css has the following rule:  ul.dnnActions input{display:none}    I can't see a good reason why real buttons (i.e. input[type=submit] and input[type=submit]) would be hidden here, rather than just styled like the links are. (It'd also be nice if the <button> element was also styled the same way)   In addition to just being unexpected, it's unfortunate because real buttons are much better supported by the browser, ASP.NET, and are more semantic.         Browser don't generally support pressing the spacebar to trigger a link.     The DefaultButton property of the asp:Panel control doesn't support LinkButtons.      Using input[type=submit] works even when JavaScript is disabled, but link buttons don't work at all without JavaScript (and aren't semantic, because they aren't linking anywhere, or acting as anchors on the page)  I understand that there are historical reasons why DNN prefers to use LinkButtons throughout the framework, but it would be great if there could at least be support for 3rd party developers to use real buttons without having to rewrite the form pattern CSS."""

description: """Traditionally, both  Module Controls and Skin objects were developed as user controls.  In order to provide developers greater flexibility and reduce redundancies, the module injection code was modified to allow web controls to be used as a module control. There are some web controls in DotNetNuke which are useful when building skins and it would be helpful if they were able to be used directly as a skin object which could be added to any HTML or ASCX skin page. Because of this change, the url is not converted to a friendly version anymore. The change happened in the method """"GetQueryStringDictionary"""". The path used to be converted to lowercase first, before checking if it contained """"login"""". Because the url contains """"Login"""", it can't make the match with """"login"""" anymore.             if ((parts.Length == 2))             {                 foreach (string part in parts[1].Split('&'))                 {                     string[] keyvalue = part.Split('=');                     if ((keyvalue.Length == 2))                     {                         results[keyvalue[0]] = keyvalue[1];                     }                 }             }               return results;         }   ....  var queryStringDic = GetQueryStringDictionary(path); ....... ......                         if (queryStringDic.ContainsKey(""""ctl"""") && !queryStringDic.ContainsKey(""""language""""))                         {                             switch (queryStringDic[""""ctl""""])                             {                                 case.........                                 case """"login"""": --> THIS CASE WILL NEVER BE HIT, because url contains """"Login""""                                      if ((queryStringDic.ContainsKey(""""returnurl"""")))                                     {                                         friendlyPath = GetFriendlyAlias(""""~/login.aspx?ReturnUrl="""" + queryStringDic[""""returnurl""""], portalAlias, isPagePath);                                     }"""

title: "Module Settings - Output, Not Output per Device Detection"
description: """As of 6.01.05 with the addition of       Back-Ported the Site Redirection Management Module to CE     Migrated from the WURFL device data repository to the 51Degrees data repository   We now have a very easy path to dramatically extend the functionality of DNN via a simple enhancement to the Module Settings.   Maybe using a pattern similar to module permissions, we should be able to decide whether the module gets output (executed) based on the device making the page request.   Here is a simple example, most sites have a significant home page Banner module. In 90% or more of cases this module should be skipped if the target device IsMobile. Conversely, many mobile sites have a """"Tap to Call Us"""" - this module should output ONLY if the device IsMobile (or CanMakePhoneCalls) and otherwise stay hidden.   Besides usefulness, this has a major impact on bandwidth usage and performance. Many modern sites are outputting significant KBs at devices with low bandwidth and this would prevent the growing situations where site developers are sending the content and then using CSS media to just hide (display:none) the stuff the device should hide. Depending on the site/page complexity, not executing N modules could be a significant server-side performance improvement."""

There are multiple issues with this design:       From a security point of view, executable code should not be stored in the user document area. title: "RadManager and ClientCapability modules cannot be set as premium"
description: """Someone is adding new providers to Dotnetnuke and is doing something wrong that doesn't allow them to be edited and set as Premium so that they can be assigned, or removed from portals as all other modules can.   The Rad Editor Manager has been like this for a while and I'v ealready reported it, but now there's a new DotNetNuke Client Capability Provider in DNN 6.1.5 that also has this problem.   It is bad because now we have a module called """"RadEditorManager"""" and a module called """"DotNetNuke Client Capability Provider"""" on every page editor's module dropdown. They can add these modules to any page, even though they have no business and no purpose in doing so. And even worse, they gain access to the settings and can screw things up for the entire DNN instance. Why would anyone give these modules to page editors, or even admins, when they are host functions.    Yet as Host we are unable to hide or remove the modules from the menu, let alone from DNN, as the DotNetNuke Client Capability Provider cannot even be deleted.   If these things are going to be added to DNN as modules, then make them editable in the same manner as all modules normally are, so that we can set them as Premium modules and therefore unavailable to portal users.   This issue is meaningless for solo-site-operators, but for anyone like myself with a full heirarchy of editors, this is a showstopper problem with the 6.1.5 upgrade.  Whoever created these packages needs to revise them and turn them into proper modules, or ensure they don't show up as modules.. either way will work."""

title: "Messaging - Real time updating does not work"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: As a user I expect that when someone sends me a message via """"Message Center"""" my Inbox updates without any input from me.  Clear Steps to Reproduce: 1. Install 6.2.0.1074 as a web site in IIS 2. Log in as HOST 3. Create a couple of users 4. Add message center to a new or existing page and permission page to be viewed by """"Registered Users"""" 5. In a different browser log into the site as one of the """"new users"""" 6. Send a message to Admin or one of the other """"new users"""" 7. Log into site in a different browser as one of the message recipients 8. Reply to the message  Actual Result: 1. No matter how long the user (initial message sender) from Step #6 waits their UI never updates unless they click the breadcrumb for the page or hit F5 to force a page refresh   Expected Result: 1. when the reply is sent that user (from Step #6) receives the message and their """"Message Center"""" UI is magically updated"""

title: "Ensure no deprecated methods point to Testablexxx Controllers"
description: """With the introduction of some internal testable controllers we accidentally deprecated some methods and pointed to replacements in the Testable versions of the controllers. We need to search (grep) for such methods and ensure that they have a public alternative available."""

title: "ContentController.GetContentItemsByTerm is ambiguous across vocabularies"
description: """The method ContentController.GetContentItemsByTerm(string) generates a set of content items by term name.  However, this term name is not guaranteed to be unique across vocabularies, and is thereby dangerously ambiguous.   This method should be replaced by three overloads:   ContentController.GetContentItemsByTerm(Term term)     {     Requires.NotNullOrEmpty(""""term"""", term);       return CBO.FillQueryable<ContentItem>(_dataService.GetContentItemsByTermId(term.TermId));     }   ContentController.GetContentItemsByTerm(Vocabulary vocabulary, string termName)     { return GetContentItemsByTerm(vocabulary.Terms.First(term => term.Name == termName)); }    ContentController.GetContentItemsByTerm(int  vocabularyId, string termName); { return GetContentItemsByTerm(new VocabularyController().GetVocabularies().First(vocabulary => vocabulary.VocabularyId == vocabularyId), termName); }   An additional dataprovider method IDataService.GetContentItemsByTermId would be introduced as:    public IDataReader GetContentItemsByTerm(int termId) { return _provider.ExecuteReader(""""GetContentItemsByTermId"""", termId); }    And the SQL is straightforward:    CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[GetContentItemsByTermId]  @TermID int AS BEGIN DECLARE @TermLeft int, @TermRight int, @VocabularyID int    SELECT   @TermLeft = TermLeft, @TermRight = TermRight, @VocabularyID = VocabularyID  FROM   dbo.Taxonomy_Terms  WHERE   TermID = @TermId    IF @TermLeft = 0 AND @TermRight = 0  BEGIN   -- Simple Term   SELECT c.*   FROM dbo.ContentItems As c    INNER JOIN dbo.ContentItems_Tags ct ON ct.ContentItemID = c.ContentItemID    INNER JOIN dbo.Taxonomy_Terms t ON t.TermID = ct.TermID   WHERE t.TermID = @TermID  END ELSE BEGIN   -- Hierarchical Term   SELECT c.*   FROM dbo.ContentItems As c    INNER JOIN dbo.ContentItems_Tags ct ON ct.ContentItemID = c.ContentItemID    INNER JOIN dbo.Taxonomy_Terms t ON t.TermID = ct.TermID   WHERE t.TermLeft >= @TermLeft    AND t.TermRight <= @TermRight    AND t.VocabularyID = @VocabularyID  END END"""

I could not only get this to work as expected if the following logic is assumed:  (a) Log into page with journal module (b) Enter URL www.cnn.com into the journal module (c) Wait. Type some more stuff - whatever.  The scrape will work with a little patience.  However if you change the scenario like this.  (a) Log into page with journal module (b) Enter URL www.cnn.com (c) Press """"Share"""" as fast as possible  The scrape (display of CNN logo etc) will not come down later.  EXPECTED:  Scrape process continues after pressing submit button (like facebook). Ideally an animation appears that indicates something is going on (like a clock timer).  ACTUAL (and this is the bug).  Press submit too quick for the scrape to happen and it won't. title: "Banner dates get reset to previous values"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: Changing the dates on a banner doesn't stick. (This might be related to DNN-14856)   Clear Steps to Reproduce:  1. Open Vendors page.  2. Select a Vendor. 3. Select a banner. 4. Change the start date or end date. 5. Click update. 6. The screen redisplays the list of banners, and the dates look okay. 7. Exit the page, re-enter Banners.   Actual Result:  1. The old dates are back.    Expected Result:  1. The entered dates should be there.  Additional Notes:  In my production web site, I wanted to change the dates on a banner. There was a problem with this-week�s banner, so I tried to set its end-date to yesterday, and set next-week�s banner to begin yesterday. Next week�s start date changed just fine.   I can tell in the database that this week�s enddate gets updated, but is immediately reverted back to the previous enddate. I have set up a query in SQL Server that returns the current week's banner dates.  As soon as I update the banner through DNN, I ran the query and confirmed that my dates were there.  A few seconds later, I reran the query, and the old dates were back.  There is a stored procedure called UpdateBannerViews that updates the Views counter, as well as the start and end dates. What I believe is happening is that users in the web site have grabbed the current week�s banner object, and the app is attempting to update the Views counter at the same time I change the date. The app is re-storing the old date (which I just changed) when all it really needs to do is increment the counter. The DNN method LoadBanners (in BannerController.cs) has some logic paths where it will assign dates if they are not already set. I contend that the dates should not be updated in the stored procedure unless the method actually needs to change them.   My work-around was to set the banner�s Impressions value to a low number, greater than 0. That told it to move on to the next video. Still, I wasted a lot of time trying to get the bad video out of the loop.  Hope this helps."""

title: "Updating Email Notification Settings For Event Log Sets NotificationThresholdTimeType to NULL"
description: """When trying to update email notifiation settings for a log event the NotificationThresholdTimeType field in the database table EventLogConfig is set to NULL.  The method in question is: UpdateLogTypeConfigInfo(LogTypeConfigInfo logTypeConfig)  in the class: DotNetNuke.Services.Log.EventLog.LogController The line: Convert.ToString(logTypeConfig.NotificationThresholdTimeType) should be: Convert.ToString((int)logTypeConfig.NotificationThresholdTimeType) Without the cast the string value of the enum is used.  Then the next method called fails.    The next method in question is: UpdateLogTypeConfigInfo  In the class: DotNetNuke.Services.Log.EventLog.DBLoggingProvider  Initially the thresholdtimetype is set to -1 int intThresholdTimeType = -1;  The method property thresholdTimeType is a string which is set in the previous class as the value of the Enum.  The regex check then fails as this can't be set to a number, and thus the threshold is left as -1 and the database sets this to be null. if(Regex.IsMatch(thresholdTimeType, """"^\\d+$"""")) { intThresholdTimeType = Convert.ToInt32(thresholdTimeType); }"""

title: "Page-Level CSS"
description: """This is probably a simple enhancement, but would provide MAJOR benefits.   We need a way to add custom CSS to a page without needing a custom Skin or some workaround like adding stylesheet references in the <head> using the page Head settings.   I envision being able to use the """"Page"""" option in the Control Panel then click on """"Page CSS"""" and it opens a text box to enter CSS into. Pretty simple.   The CSS would have to be registered with the Client Dependency Framework of course so it is merged.   I would guess it should be loaded just before the Portal CSS file as I believe the intention of the Portal CSS file is to override everything at a portal level.   I would also like to see possibly two TABS, one for CSS and the other for .LESS which I proposed quite a while ago.  The .LESS box, if not empty, would be used and the CSS box would be populated with the .LESS output. That's not 100% necessary, but nice to be able to see the .LESS' CSS output. A checkbox would be necessary to know which to use, CSS or LESS. I suppose since .LESS hasnt made it into DNN yet, this would come later, but should be thought of at this stage anyways.   When saving page CSS, it should increment the CDF version as well.   Taking a step further, this could also be implemented at the module level. In this manner, a site admin can MODIFY a module's """"module.css"""" file giving complete control. Otherwise, the site admin needs to bring down the project, modify or remove the module.css file, repackage and reinstall. Total pain for interface designers. Not practical. Therefore, any module which contains a module.css file will be given a new action menu called """"Module CSS"""". Again, A .LESS implementation here would be monumental to allow enterprise developers to piggyback off of the MAIN .LESS implementation for the Portal or Page *IF* the .LESS CSS output was compiled as ONE .css file instead of multiples for Portal, Page, Module etc...  That way, .LESS functions and inheritance can cascade and be used all the way down the line.   Since I implement mainly in the enterprise environment, I also believe this should all integrate in a manner that allows ALL portals to use an enterprise .LESS CSS output file if possible.  Would need to be a host-level setting.   Even though I mentioned .LESS a lot here, the main enhancement was the Page CSS and subsequently Module CSS features which should be the focus when evaluating this enhancement request.   Thanks guys!!!   <USER>""

title: "Translations of ""Like"" in Journal"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: In the resource files for the Journal module there are a couple entries that are used to build a whole sentence. For example,  {resx:likesthis}.Text => """"likes this""""  this will be used in the module to build a setence like: """"Joe User likes this""""  The problem is that is some languages the correct sentence requires a prefix, or maybe the name should go after. For example:  In spanish that would be: """"A Joe User le gusta""""  Solution: the resource key should be a format string like:  {resx:likesthis}.Text => """"{0} likes this""""  So translators have more flexibility with this."""

title: "Refactoring client resource files"
description: """Summary: Leverage the abilities of Client Resource Manager to refactor how CSS and JS files are served and customized per portal.  Problem Description: The current method for serving resource files relies on global files that only allow customization and control through: 1) changing the source files which affects all portals and creates upgrade issues, and 2) writing bloated skin/container code to reset the core.    Resetting is troublesome since some CSS properties can�t be removed without artifacts that must be fixed with further code.  The process raises the bar for skills needed to successfully skin a site.   A few third party extensions allow skin designers to programmatically remove core file but this means carefully transferring parts of the core code lest some extension wouldn't look or work correctly.    Upgrades to portals with these extensions wouldn�t get any changes such as the addition of the jQuery UI recently.  Maintenance became a more laborious, technical task.    Important DNN creates a system that allows it to shift with prevalent Internet standards and paradigms.  Accordingly, the UX patterns which are mostly generic and semantic would allow different UI libraries.  However, the current method is rigidly coupled with jQuery UI.  By designing the patterns around a more pluggable UI system, the platform becomes more �future ready�    The reliance on the default.css file means it has grown in size and contains code that most users will never need.  Further, it is littered with declarations the bind the hands of designers � a fact that is often discovered after much frustration.  It makes too many decisions for the designer thus reducing their ability to adopt emerging coding standards.    Problem Summary:        System requires bloated and redundant code for design customization     Legacy choices make skinning needlessly difficult.     System is rigidly tied to one UI library.     Lighter methods of customization break the upgrade path.     A good deal of the code sent to the user isn't used.     System isn't flexible enough to support changes in the industry    Proposed Solution: The needs of the designers, portal administrators, and ultimately end users could be better addressed by a refactoring of the core CSS and JS files.  The maturing of the Client Resource Manager (CRM) provides an opportunity to replace the current system with a far more robust and adaptable one.    Central to the solution is to treat the portal root as equivalent to the website root from the CRM point of view.  This would allow portal specific files to override the global version for full control over the final design.   [footnote: if the enhancement consideration below is added, then /Portals/0/css/settings.css file containing the variables would be all that is required to style the UI.]    Further, as the CRM can combining files, the Default.css file should be broken up into as many functional components as possible. This will aid in maintenance and debugging without affecting the end product.  Maintenance is assisted as customizations are isolated from module and extension content. For instance, an override of default.css need not touch the specific code for the tags module.  The tags module would be able to upgrade without interfering with the customizations.   To avoid backward compatibility issues, the CRM should pull resources from a new, global /CSS/ folder. Those that opt to not use the CRM will use the current default.css and avoid any issues.   If a /CSS/ folder is present in the portal root, the files in it will override the global counterparts.  A similar concept could work for the /JS/ folder.   The final piece to give designers full control would be a mechanism to remove assets from the skins.   With all of these in place, a designer wouldn't have to override or patch the default styles nearly as much.  They could achieve unique designs without impacting other portals or upgrades.    ENHANCEMENT CONSIDERATION As the CRM can use extensions, the inclusion of a LESS or SASS style parsing engine would allow easy restyling of all DNN parts.    These CSS parsers enable variables and other shortcuts which could become part of the code patterns.  For instance, instead of a module developer setting the font size in pixels, they would use the @BodyFont variable.  Of course, that would mean a parser is required which may be too much of a commitment to a non-WC3 concept."""

title: "Reusable Components - move images and css to the template level"
description: """Right now the component (e.g. Resources/Shared/Components/MyComponent/) is structured as follows:         Images     Templates     MyComponent.css     MyComponent.js  The problem with this is that the images, css and template all work together but aren't """"scoped"""" together.    We should do it like this:         Templates              Default                      Images             style.css                                 UserFileManager.js  Additionally, the template should be responsible for loading *both* the JS and the CSS for the template dynamically. That way the """"consumer"""" only needs to register the JS file and initialize the plugin, the rest is taken care of."""

title: "Countrynames are not localized (and not localizable)"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: Countries codes and names are stored in the Lists table. Regrettably, when this feature was implemented in a distant past, it was somehow decided to use CountryNames instead of CountryCodes in the userProfile. Of course this causes a couple of issues:       when the name of a country changes, but not the country code, there is no way to easily update this (other than by doing a db script on the userprofile table     in multilingual sites, you would want the name of the country to be localized in the current language. When using country codes that is relatively easy, when using full names that is impossible  IMO 2 things need to happen:       The List Table needs to become content localizable (ie. it needs a culturecode column)     the user profile needs to switch from full country name to country code.  The latter will pose a problem during an upgrade, which we can counteract by running a sql script that looks up the country in the lists table, and replaces the full country name with the country code in the userprofile table"""

title: "Faulty and Unexpected Error Handling Behavior"
description: """Brief Description of Issue:  The way that DNN handles and displays exceptions when they're caught and passed to either the ProcessModuleLoadException or ProcessPageLoadException methods is pretty solid. Humor me and follow my thoughts as I step through the logic below:   An external entity obviously can't directly invoke a call to the ProcessModuleLoadException static method. They'd have to exploit some vulnerability in the CMS or a custom module to cause an exception to be thrown. But, there just one thing about the ProcessModuleLoadException; if you don't have the Use Custom Error Messages host setting checked, then the exception is simply thrown, propagating up the call stack and finally being caught by the OnError method of the PageBase class . Also, same thing goes for the ProcessPageLoadException method. This is all reasonable.     If UseCustomErrorMessages is true, error messages are shown to all users (authenticated and unauthenticated) for after passing caught exceptions to both ProcessModuleLoadException and ProcessPageLoadException. If you are an admin user you see the full exception message, otherwise you get generic exception message (unless you use the overload of ProcessModuleLoadException that accepts """"friendlymessage"""" as the first parameter). Perfect. ProcessPageLoadException calls do appear to cause a redirect loop in DNN 6+ for both authenticated and unauthenticated users when UseCustomErrorMessages is true. <-- something worth looking into maybe *shrug*     If UseCustomErrorMessages is false, calls to ProcessModuleLoadException and ProcessPageLoadException result in unauthenticated and non-admin users not seeing any error messages at all (even if the friendlymessage overload of ProcessModuleLoadException is called or if the DisplayErrorMessage is explicitly set to true). This could deceive the user into believing there is nothing wrong with the module and that their transaction had gone through with no problem. <-- something to think about.   If UseCustomErrorMessages is false, generic """"{modulename} is currently unavailable"""" message is shown to admin users after calls to ProcessModuleLoadException. ProcessPageLoadException calls show the actual exception message to admins. <-- seems inconsistent with the behavior of ProcessModuleLoadException.       On to uncaught exceptions. If UseCustomErrorMessages is false, no error message is displayed to unauthenticated and non-admin users. This is troublesome because if admins don't regularly go through the EventViewer they'll never know uncaught exceptions are occurring and neither with normal users because they can't see them and they can't report the message. In the past I've setup Daily Exception Report SSRS reports against staging sites going through the client QA phase. This was very beneficial...but an incredible amount of overhead required to do it. What I'm getting at is that I believe even if UseCustomErrorMessages is false, some form of an error message should be displayed to non-admins and unauthenticated users.   Now here's the interesting part. The above behavior for uncaught exceptions is only valid (as far as I can tell from my testing) during PageInit. Uncaught exceptions thrown during PageLoad while UseCustomErrorMessages will get propagated up to the OnError handler of the PageBase class and the user will get redirected to a URL with the """"error"""" parameter and will simply render whatever is specified in that URL parameter. <-- I know I'm starting to get picky, but all that needs to happen is one savvy user see that they can manipulate the content of the page via a URL parameter to start going wild. title: "Performance enhancement for (deprecated) function that is used by many older navigation providers"
description: """The TabController.GetTab and TabController.GetTabByParentId methods are deprecated, but are nonetheless used by older navigation providers that have not yet been updated.  They are the only deprecated methods that continue to make direct DAL calls; other similar methods rely upon the new entity caching that was introduced in the 6.x line.   A small change to these methods yields a gigantic performance benefit; in my ad hoc experiment, a single server was able to process more than 10x more requests per second after this modification was introduced.   Suggest modifying the methods as:    [Obsolete(""""This method is obsolete.  It has been replaced by GetTab(ByVal TabId As Integer, ByVal PortalId As Integer, ByVal ignoreCache As Boolean) """")] public TabInfo GetTab(int TabId)     {     return GetTab(TabId, GetPortalId(TabId, Null.NullInteger), false);     }     [Obsolete(""""This method is obsolete.  It has been replaced by GetTabsByParent(ByVal ParentId As Integer, ByVal PortalId As Integer) """")] public ArrayList GetTabsByParentId(int ParentId)     {     return new ArrayList(GetTabsByParent(ParentId, GetPortalId(ParentId, Null.NullInteger)));     }    Many of the other deprecated methods already exist in a form similar to the above."""

title: "ServiceLocator initialization is not thread-safe"
description: """Looking over Charles' blog, I noted that the initialization logic of ServiceLocator is not thread-safe, and two ill-timed requests will cause mischief if the resultant controller expects to maintain shared state.   Suggest modifying to read (changes in bold):  private static object _lock = new Object(); public static TContract Instance         {             get             {                  //ignore potential races                 //it is not a big deal if two instances are occaisionally created                  // Yes it is, when you least expect it.              lock(_lock)             {                 if (!_isInitialized)                 {                     if (Factory == null)                     {                         var controllerInstance = new TSelf();                         Factory = controllerInstance.GetFactory();                     }                      _instance = Factory();                     _isInitialized = true;                 }                  return _instance;             }         }  }   This abstraction also implies that all controllers exposed through it are thread-safe, which may result in all sorts of subtle fun!"""

title: "Use of CurrentCulture and CurrentUICulture cause inconsistencies in UI"
description: """Context: Multiple language packs installed and content localization activated   Brief Description of Issue: Logged on users, in edit mode, will not see the localized interface, as per this description on the DotNetNuke wiki: http://www.dotnetnuke.com/Resources/Wiki/Page/Localization-logic.aspx    The problem is that we are using CurrentCulture to localize the content, and CurrentUICulture to localize the interface. However, there is no way to change the CurrentUICulture.   The problem here is that we tried to fix something that was only mildly broken, and we fixed it with something that is very much broken. There are 2 use cases:   * an admin wants to edit a different language on the page, and uses the language selector on the page to change its language. For his convenience, the interface stays in the same language, but the content of the module can now be edited in the other language. * the same admin wants to do an admin task and goes to any of the admin or host menus. He wants to use the interface in a different language than the site is currently in. he is not able to do that, since there is no way to change the interface language   The easy solution would be to make the currentculture and currentUIculture in sync again, with the following effects: * if you want to edit content in a different language, the language of the interface will also change * you will now be able to view the interface in the right language     So the proposal is to fix this in the short term by syncing CurrentCulture and CurrentUICulture. The long term solution (enhancement) would be this: * add an option for admins to either sync or not sync currentCulture and currentUICulture * by default both are synced * i they are non synced, the control panel will get an extra language selector that allows editors to select the interface language seperately"""

title: "Inconsistent friendly URI handling for HTTPS and non-port-80 requests"
description: """The behavior of Globals.NavigateURL is inconsistent between an HTTP and HTTPS version of an otherwise identical URI due to an unintended comparison in the core friendly URL provider and in the Globals.AddPort method.  As a result, non-HTTP requests on ports other than 80 will be similarly affected.   In FriendlyUrlProvider.GetFriendlyAlias on or about line 296, a match is attempted between a given portal alias and the originally requested URI:    string httpAlias = Globals.AddHTTP(portalAlias).ToLowerInvariant(); string originalUrl = HttpContext.Current.Items[""""UrlRewrite:OriginalUrl""""].ToString().ToLowerInvariant(); httpAlias = Globals.AddPort(httpAlias, originalUrl); if (originalUrl.StartsWith(httpAlias))     ... Return a URI with this alias attached // Otherwise, return a relative path    The behavior of Globals.AddPort (line 1097) is a little strange, in that it handles port-80 as a special case:    var uri = new Uri(originalUrl); var aliasUri = new Uri(httpAlias);   if (uri.Port != 80)     httpAlias = AddHTTP(aliasUri.Host + """":"""" + uri.Port + aliasUri.LocalPath);   Now consider an HTTPS request for the URI """"https://dotnetnuke.com/mypage"""":   httpAlias [Initial] = """"https://dotnetnuke.com""""  originalUrl = """"https://dotnetnuke.com/mypage"""" httpAlias [after Globals.AddPort] = """"https://dotnetnuke:443"""" originalUrl.StartsWith(httpAlias) = False   Our conditional thereby erroneously fails, and a relative path is returned.   Because of this, we obtain inconsistent results between HTTP and HTTPS versions of the same call.  E.g.,    NavigateUrl(""""http://dotnetnuke.com/mypage"""") = """"http://dotnetnuke.com/mypage"""" NavigateUrl(""""https://dotnetnuke.com/mypage"""") = """"/mypage""""   This is silly, and I suggest correcting in one of two ways.       1. The higher risk change is to alter the behavior in Globals.AddPort to observe well-known protocols:    private static readonly IDictionary<string, int> SchemeMap =             new Dictionary<string, int>                 {                 {Uri.UriSchemeFile, -1},                 {Uri.UriSchemeFtp, 21},                 {Uri.UriSchemeGopher, 70},                 {Uri.UriSchemeHttp, 80},                 {Uri.UriSchemeHttps, 443},                 {Uri.UriSchemeMailto, 25},                 {Uri.UriSchemeNetPipe, -1},                 {Uri.UriSchemeNetTcp, 808},                 {Uri.UriSchemeNntp, 119},                 };     public static string AddPort(string httpAlias, string originalUrl) { ...   var uri = new Uri(originalUrl); var aliasUri = new Uri(httpAlias);   if(!SchemeMap.TryGetValue(uri.Scheme, out defaultPort) || uri.Port != defaultPort)     httpAlias = AddHTTP(aliasUri.Host + """":"""" + uri.Port + aliasUri.LocalPath); ... }   2. Make the minimum, half-assed change to Globals.AddPort to fix this specific issue:     if((uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttp && uri.Port != 80) || (uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttps && uri.Port != 443))        httpAlias = AddHTTP(aliasUri.Host + """":"""" + uri.Port + aliasUri.LocalPath);   3. Ignore the Globals.AddPort issue entirely and just sidestep the issue in the friendly URL provider:    private string GetFriendlyAlias(string path, string portalAlias, bool isPagePath)  { ...  if (HttpContext.Current.Items[""""UrlRewrite:OriginalUrl""""] != null)     {     string httpAlias = Globals.AddHTTP(portalAlias).ToLowerInvariant();     string originalUrl = HttpContext.Current.Items[""""UrlRewrite:OriginalUrl""""].ToString().ToLowerInvariant();     httpAlias = Globals.AddPort(httpAlias, originalUrl);     originalUrl = Globals.AddPort(originalUrl, originalUrl);     if (originalUrl.StartsWith(httpAlias))          ...     ...     } ... }   Solution #3 makes me sad inside."""

title: "Allow control panels to explicitly control their addition to control hierarchy"
description: """In Skin.InjectControlPanel (on or about line 274), a control panel is loaded and attached to the control hierarchy.  For unauthorized users, we expect that the visibility bit of the control will be cleared and no markup will be ultimately transmitted by this control.   However, given that the preponderance of requests to a site will not result in a visible control panel, the (very) high cost associated with attaching the control to the page hierarchy results in a severe performance penalty.   To remedy this issue, I suggest allowing control panels to specify whether they would like to be attached to the page control hierarchy by introducing a property in ControlPanelBase:    public virtual bool IncludeInControlHierarchy     { get { return true; } }    Note that for compatibility reasons we default to true so that existing control panels will behave as they did previously.  Similarly, control panels can (and should) continue to perform additional authorization checks within their event handlers, as has always been the case.   Concrete control panels can modify the resulting bit based upon contextual authorization.  For example, the property should be overridden in RibbonBar.ascx.cs to read:    public override bool IncludeInControlHierarchy     { get { return base.IncludeInControlHierarchy && (IsPageAdmin() || IsModuleAdmin()); } }    Finally, we adjust the InjectControlPanel method in Skin.cs (on or about line 274) to consider this property:    //ControlPanel processing var objControlPanel = ControlUtilities.LoadControl<ControlPanelBase>(this, Host.ControlPanel);   //inject ControlPanel control into skin if (!objControlPanel.IncludeInControlHierarchy)     return; else if (ControlPanel == null)      ...   This is a very low-impact change, since it will not affect behavior for existing control panels.  However, in my analysis I see a 20-40% improvement in page throughput under stress.   This is a very big performance win for a very small change.  I suggest its immediate consideration."""

Concrete control panels can modify the resulting bit based upon contextual authorization. For example, the property should be overridden in RibbonBar.ascx.cs to read: public override bool IncludeInControlHierarchy { get { return base.IncludeInControlHierarchy && (IsPageAdmin() || IsModuleAdmin()); } } Finally, we adjust the InjectControlPanel method in Skin.cs (on or about line 274) to consider this property: //ControlPanel processing var objControlPanel = ControlUtilities.LoadControl<ControlPanelBase>(this, Host.ControlPanel); //inject ControlPanel control into skin if (!objControlPanel.IncludeInControlHierarchy) return; else if (ControlPanel == null) ... This is a very low-impact change, since it will not affect behavior for existing control panels. However, in my analysis I see a 20-40% improvement in page throughput under stress. This is a very big performance win for a very small change. I suggest its immediate consideration.""

title: "The text and heading of the ModuleMessage skin object can't be set within an event handler."

If the skin object were to not use Label server controls for the heading and message text components, and were set via <%= %> code blocks within the markup, the Text and Heading properties could be set during any event of the lifecycle before Render. Set the """"Text"""" or """"Heading"""" property of an instance of the ModuleMessage skin object during a button's click event.  2.  Actual Result: 1. The module message renders with no text. 2. description: """DNN 6.1 has changed the behavior of the install process in that it does not create the admin account.  Instead it assigns the host account as the default administrator to the portal.  This change will cause problems with modules that rely on an admin account that is not a super user.    This behavior is not only destructive to some modules, it also it creates additional work creating an admin account after install and then assigning it as the default portal admin, as rarly will you give host rights to a user.  The install process should revert back to the 6.0.x way."""

title: "Access Denied Pages - Removal of the ""message"" URL parameter"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: The AccessDenied control (found within the /admin/Security/ directory) accepts a """"message"""" URL parameter that allows any custom message to be displayed within the modules default message banner. While I realize this behavior is not an actual """"bug"""", I also feel that it exposes to malicious users the ability to fabricate inappropriate page content that can then be propagated throughout the internet and quite easily picked up by Search Engine spiders and become listed in high ranking search results. This has in fact happened to a client of mine (a municipality no less) and it is quite embarrassing. We've since gone into the source code and removed this capability. I believe this functionality should be removed from the core code base.   Clear Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a URL as such: /{pagename}/tabid/{tabid}/ctl/Access%20Denied/Default.aspx?message={inappropriate_message}   Actual Result: 1. Displayed to the user is the inappropriate message fabricated by the malicious user.   Expected Result: 1. Same"""

title: "Assemblies wrongly registered on DNN3 manifest modules"
description: """I finally found out what has been bugging a bunch of my customers. The problem is that DNN does not copy in a new dll from the install zip because it believes the current dll to be of a higher version. But this is not true. The real issue is that if you install a module with a DNN 3 manifest ALL included assemblies are assumed to have the SAME version number. So in my case a shared lib was registered as v 5.x whereas it was 2.x.   Solution 1: Reflection. I know this doesn't work in partial trust but the code could try. And if this doesn't work ...   Solution 2: Don't register the assembly!   And please include some upgrade code in the core to reparse existing assemblies and set their version correctly. The error has my customers reeling. This needs to be fixed."""

title: "Tab icon paths broken in portal template"
description: """Tab Icon paths in portal templates created by DNN 6 contain portal IDs, causing them to be broken in new portals created from the template.  In portal templates created by DNN 3/4/5, tab iconfiles were correctly recorded with paths relative to the portal root, as follows:  <tab>  <iconfile>Icons/myicon.png</iconfile> </tab>  In templates created by DNN 6, the iconfile paths are now relative to the system root, as follows:  <tab>  <iconfile>/Portals/57/Icons/myicon.png</iconfile> </tab>  I would assume this also to be the case for the large tab icons.  This means that any new portal created from this template is referencing icons that may or may not even be there.  To reproduce this, simply apply a tab icon to a page, export the portal as a template and then examine the iconfile paths in the template file.   Obviously, a template should never refer to a path that is unique to the original portal. It should always be relative to the new portal.  The solution will be to restore this back to the way it was in DNN 3/4/5 and remove """"/Portals/xx/"""" from the recorded path."""

title: "Module control keys with spaces will cause Popup setting to always be True"
description: """A module which has a space in the ControlKey of a control, and with popups set to false will not have the popup setting honoured.       NavigateURL will converts the controlkey to be part an HTML encoded part of the URL, e.g. 'Feedback Moderation' will become 'Feedback%20Moderation'.     ModuleAction.Add  through new ModuleAction/ControlKey will set the controlkey of the module action to 'Feedback%20Moderation' by extracting it from the url     IsLegacyUI in UIUtilities looks up the SupportsPopUps setting of the control using this ControlKey. title: "Move module to another page loses pane assignment"
description: """Moving a module to another page leaves the module without a content pane assignment.   This causes a variety of problems, including that the module then doesn't respond to up/down actions within the pane, nor does it pick up any pane-assigned containers.  To demonstrate the bug, here in DNN 6.1.2, do the following:      Create a site with two pages: page 1 and page 2     Place an HTML module into """"ContentPane"""" on page 1     View the action menu of the HTML module     You will observe that """"ContentPane"""" does not exist as a """"Move"""" destination, because the module is already there.     Edit that module's settings     Go to Page Settings, Advanced Settings     Select """"Move to page"""" and choose page 2     Click Update     Navigate to page 2     View the action menu of the HTML module you moved here     You will observe that """"ContentPane"""" now exists as a """"Move"""" destination     That confirms that the module has not been assigned to """"ContentPane""""     If you had several modules in this pane, you would not be able to move this module up and down in relation to them     You must instead """"Move"""" the module to """"ContentPane"""" first     Then it will respond to up/down movements  The behaviour in DNN3/4/5 was that any module moved to another page would land in the same content area that it was in on the source page. If that content pane did not exist on the target page, then it would be placed in the default """"ContentPane"""" pane. In DNN 6, it always lands without any pane assigned."""

Edit that module's settings Go to Page Settings, Advanced Settings Select """"Move to page"""" and choose page 2 Click Update Navigate to page 2 View the action menu of the HTML module you moved here You will observe that """"ContentPane"""" now exists as a """"Move"""" destination That confirms that the module has not been assigned to """"ContentPane"""" If you had several modules in this pane, you would not be able to move this module up and down in relation to them You must instead """"Move"""" the module to """"ContentPane"""" first Then it will respond to up/down movements The behaviour in DNN3/4/5 was that any module moved to another page would land in the same content area that it was in on the source page. If that content pane did not exist on the target page, then it would be placed in the default """"ContentPane"""" pane. In DNN 6, it always lands without any pane assigned.""

title: """Leave it alone"" option for text/html editor"
description: """Some feedback / bugs / feature enhancements for our text/html editor..   Some background... We have to Editor Modes: Basic and Rich.                 When EDITING CONTENT, you can do it in a plain text box, or in a rich text editor   We have three Render Modes: Text/Html/Raw.                 When DNN RENDERS the content, it will spit out the content as plain text, HTML or Raw       1. What is the difference between Text and Raw?                  Why do we need two?                 Maybe the tooltip could be used to explain this.                 HTML mode (I would imagine) would do the stripping of script tags, newlines, fix up the content etc..                 Switching between RENDER modes actually causes the text to go through some level of parsing                                 For example, new lines are removed                                 Why?     2. Why, when changing Render Mode, does it do a post back?                 Render mode is only concerned during DISPLAY of content, and not editing                 Doesn�t make sense and it is distracting.     3. Try this: Switch to RAW Render Mode, BASIC Editor Mode                 Enter in the following:     <img src=""""http://www.google.ca/images/srpr/logo3w.png""""> <img src=""""./images/srpr/logo3w.png"""">  <img src=""""images/srpr/logo3w.png""""> <img src=""""/images/srpr/logo3w.png"""">   Hit Save. Next notice that the SRC attributes have been mangled with what DNN """"thinks"""" they should be.     IMHO this should be considered a bug.  Tested and confirmed on both 5.6.7.4 AND 6.1.0.   Cant Raw just be Raw? DNN simply will leave it alone?   Maybe we need to add a """"Leave it alone"""" render and edit modes?"""

title: "Exceptions.LogException fails (silently) for all exceptions that occur prior to MembershipProvider component registration"
description: """Consider an exception that is thrown during the registration of a component PRIOR to registration of the MembershipProvider.  (By way of example, such an exception will occur when a logging provider assembly is removed from the bin directory but not the web.config.)   This failure will be logged in ProviderInstaller.cs on or about line 92:    Type type = BuildManager.GetType(provider.Type, false, true); if (type == null)     {     Exceptions.LogException(new ConfigurationErrorsException(string.Format(""""Could not load provider {0}"""", provider.Type)));     }    This exception will eventually attempt to gather details about the user who triggered the exception (if any), in BasePortalException.cs on or about line 170:    var currentUserInfo = UserController.GetCurrentUserInfo(); UserID = (currentUserInfo != null) ? currentUserInfo.UserID : -1;    However, since the MembershipProvider component has not yet been installed, the GetCurrentUserInfo() invocation will fail (due to its dereferencing a null membership provider).   The exception is therefore not logged and a silent (likely critical) failure occurs.   Consider omitting user details if no membership provider instance exists, as:    var currentUserInfo = MembershipProvider.Instance() != null ? UserController.GetCurrentUserInfo() : null;"""

title: "Usability Issue with Uploading Large Files: File Manager Upload and URL Control"
description: """Brief Description of Issue: When a user attempts to upload a file larger than what their site is configured to accept, they can be faced with a dead end error message.  This is not a user friendly experience.  They should instead be notified prior to upload what the file upload restrictions are, and when they are exceeded, the error should be trapped and reported back in a user friendly way with an appropriate message.   I marked this as a major issue due to the incredibly bad user experience that this presents to our non-technical users.  This bad user experience is found in our core product, supported community modules, as well as potentially any 3rd party or custom module.  Clear Steps to Reproduce: 1.  Install DNN (any latest version) 2.  Use the File Manager or any URL Control on any module to upload a large file (e.g., a HD video). Modules to try this with include Documents, Media, etc. 3.  Select the file 4.  Click the upload link/button  Actual Result: 1.  The dead end error message appears  Expected Result: 1.  There should be a user-friendly message showing the maximum allowed size of files that can be uploaded (File Manager has this, URL Control doesn't). 2.  The file should be uploaded, or the original UI should refresh with a user-friendly error shown.  The error message should ideally show the size of the file that was attempted to be uploaded compared to the size that is allowed.   File Manager > Upload: This actually keeps you on the site, but shows a horrible message on a generic error page.  Your only recourse when this happens is to return to the site home page.  As a host user, you at least have some idea of why this happened.  As any other user, you just received a generic error message that is meaningless.  That message should be more detailed in why the error happened, and it should appear in the original upload view as a typical page/module message.   URL Control > Upload: Same experience, but it doesn't display the maximum file size allowed."""

THis occurs on any control, but for our testing we typically enabled partial render on the File Manager as a test. The interesting thing is that if you continue to upgrade to 5.6.6 the error stays, but the actual error description changes.
