title: "SI: AJAX requests and Digest Auth in cross domain environment"
description: """Description: In 7.0.5 if request header X-REQUESTED-WITH: XmlHttpRequest then SupportsDigestAuth method returns false. This logic is by design however this is preventing developers from leveraging the Services Framework from web applicationsoutside of DNN. DNN 705 PE ELITE\Community\DotNetNuke.Web\Api\Internal\Auth\AuthMessageHandlerBase.cs         private const string RequestedWithHeader = """"X-REQUESTED-WITH"""";          protected static bool IsXmlHttpRequest(HttpRequestMessage request)         {             if (request.Headers.Contains(RequestedWithHeader))             {                 string header = request.Headers.GetValues(RequestedWithHeader).FirstOrDefault();                 return !String.IsNullOrEmpty(header) &&                        header.Equals(""""XmlHttpRequest"""", StringComparison.InvariantCultureIgnoreCase);             }              return false;         } DNN 705 PE ELITE\Community\DotNetNuke.Web\Api\Internal\Auth\DigestAuthMessageHandler.cs         private bool SupportsDigestAuth(HttpRequestMessage request)         {             return !IsXmlHttpRequest(request);         }         public override HttpResponseMessage OnOutboundResponse(HttpResponseMessage response, CancellationToken cancellationToken)         {             if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized && SupportsDigestAuth(response.RequestMessage))             {                 AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(response);             }             return base.OnOutboundResponse(response, cancellationToken);         }         private void AddStaleWwwAuthenticateHeader(HttpResponseMessage response)         {             AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(response, true);         }         private void AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(HttpResponseMessage response, bool isStale = false)         {             var value = string.Format(""""realm=\""""DNNAPI\"""", nonce=\""""{0}\"""",  opaque=\""""0000000000000000\"""", stale={1}, algorithm=MD5, qop=\""""auth\"""""""", CreateNewNonce(), isStale);             response.Headers.WwwAuthenticate.Add(new AuthenticationHeaderValue(""""Digest"""", value));         } Below is a customer feedback: You say that this logic is by design however this is preventingdevelopers from leveraging the Services Framework from web applicationsoutside of DNN. This is severely limiting our ability to build aservices framework using DNN that we can share with entities outside ofthe Arizona Game and Fish Department. For example, we intend on usingthese services in modules we build as well as systems that ourcontractors build for us using different technologies.   Why can't this be configurable, let the developers choose whether DigestAuthentication is supported for XmlHttpRequets? Unless there is atechnical reason that you can explain, it seems a rather arbitrarydecision or one designed to purposely limit our choices.   Scott S has confirmed this: """"The check for the x-requested-with was header was to prevent digest and basic auth from running when a browser is making a request.  If the a browser request is un-authenticated, and the basic and/or digest auth test fails, it will insert the auth headers into the response which will cause the browser to pop-up it's ugly built-in credentials dialog which we do not want. I did not test any cross domain situations.  Off the top of my head I can't think of a better way to separate browser requests from AJAX requests (I know it is possible to make an AJAX request without the header but most AJAX libraries will include it).  I would suggest that the developer adjust their client to include the header in the request.  That should be an easy work around until someone can think up a better solution to avoiding the browsers built-in authentication dialogs. Scott S."""" """"Our first pass on Service Framework was intended to support within-DNN uses, as there are more potential issues with external to DNN uses, so I am ok with opening this up for 7.1 <USER>DotNetNuke Corporation""""    """

Title: SI: AJAX requests and Digest Auth in cross domain environment
Description: ""Description: In 7.0.5 if request header X-REQUESTED-WITH: XmlHttpRequest then SupportsDigestAuth method returns false. This logic is by design however this is preventing developers from leveraging the Services Framework from web applicationsoutside of DNN. DNN 705 PE ELITE\Community\DotNetNuke.Web\Api\Internal\Auth\AuthMessageHandlerBase.cs         private const string RequestedWithHeader = """"X-REQUESTED-WITH"""";          protected static bool IsXmlHttpRequest(HttpRequestMessage request)         {             if (request.Headers.Contains(RequestedWithHeader))             {                 string header = request.Headers.GetValues(RequestedWithHeader).FirstOrDefault();                 return !String.IsNullOrEmpty(header) &&                        header.Equals(""""XmlHttpRequest"""", StringComparison.InvariantCultureIgnoreCase);             }              return false;         } DNN 705 PE ELITE\Community\DotNetNuke.Web\Api\Internal\Auth\DigestAuthMessageHandler.cs         private bool SupportsDigestAuth(HttpRequestMessage request)         {             return !IsXmlHttpRequest(request);         }         public override HttpResponseMessage OnOutboundResponse(HttpResponseMessage response, CancellationToken cancellationToken)         {             if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized && SupportsDigestAuth(response.RequestMessage))             {                 AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(response);             }             return base.OnOutboundResponse(response, cancellationToken);         }         private void AddStaleWwwAuthenticateHeader(HttpResponseMessage response)         {             AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(response, true);         }         private void AddWwwAuthenticateHeader(HttpResponseMessage response, bool isStale = false)         {             var value = string.Format(""""realm=\""""DNNAPI\"""", nonce=\""""{0}\"""",  opaque=\""""0000000000000000\"""", stale={1}, algorithm=MD5, qop=\""""auth\"""""""", CreateNewNonce(), isStale);             response.Headers.WwwAuthenticate.Add(new AuthenticationHeaderValue(""""Digest"""", value));         } Below is a customer feedback: You say that this logic is by design however this is preventingdevelopers from leveraging the Services Framework from web applicationsoutside of DNN. This is severely limiting our ability to build aservices framework using DNN that we can share with entities outside ofthe Arizona Game and Fish Department. For example, we intend on usingthese services in modules we build as well as systems that ourcontractors build for us using different technologies.   Why can't this be configurable, let the developers choose whether DigestAuthentication is supported for XmlHttpRequets? Unless there is atechnical reason that you can explain, it seems a rather arbitrarydecision or one designed to purposely limit our choices.   Scott S has confirmed this: """"The check for the x-requested-with was header was to prevent digest and basic auth from running when a browser is making a request.  If the a browser request is un-authenticated, and the basic and/or digest auth test fails, it will insert the auth headers into the response which will cause the browser to pop-up it's ugly built-in credentials dialog which we do not want. I did not test any cross domain situations.  Off the top of my head I can't think of a better way to separate browser requests from AJAX requests (I know it is possible to make an AJAX request without the header but most AJAX libraries will include it).  I would suggest that the developer adjust their client to include the header in the request.  That should be an easy work around until someone can think up a better solution to avoiding the browsers built-in authentication dialogs. Scott S."""" """"Our first pass on Service Framework was intended to support within-DNN uses, as there are more potential issues with external to DNN uses, so I am ok with opening this up for 7.1 <USER>DotNetNuke Corporation""""    ""
